# The Agent OS project: vision

## In short
One paragraph: what the Agent OS is, how the owner builds it by vibecoding with the project IDE as their window, that nothing runs yet, and the current stage.

## Why we are building it
The problem (too much agent work for one person; vibecoding hides the picture), the goals as a short list, and what success looks like.

## The concept
The two halves: the system being built (agents, domains, trading, apps) and the way it is built (levels of docs, metadata next to everything, the way of working, the project IDE, the planning area), each by what it does.

## How it should work
A round of work as numbered steps, from the owner's words to a merged change, with a small picture. No paths.

## The business logic
The rules the project follows, one plain statement each: decided only on the owner's word, every input kept, a plan for every change, docs as they are now, the page equals the disk, keys never leave the machine, nothing hard to undo without the owner, work in stages.

## Examples
Two to four short worked examples: a request from the page, a change across levels, a cold session start.

## What the owner sees and does
A short list of what the owner does day to day while the project is planned and built.

## Where we are and what comes next
Honest status, stage one in numbered steps, stage two, and later plans in one paragraph.

## Principles
Rules of thumb, one or two sentences each with the reason.

## Ideas we are still weighing
For each idea: the problem, the idea, what it would change.

## Open questions
Questions only the owner can answer, each with why it matters.

## Going deeper
Two sentences naming `docs/README.md`.

nodes.content:
# The Agent OS project: vision

## In short

The Agent OS is the owner's personal system for running AI agents of any kind: agents that trade, that work on social media or that help with management. It runs many small agents side by side, each with one clear job, tries every idea safely first and keeps what works, like a wheel that keeps turning. Trading on prediction markets is its first area of work. This project is how the Agent OS gets built: the owner says what they want in plain words, and AI writes the plans, the docs and later the code, while the owner follows, understands and steers everything through their own window on the project, the project IDE. Nothing of the system runs yet. The project is in its first stage: finishing that window and writing down the whole design, clearly and completely, before the first trading agents are built in the second stage.

## Why we are building it

There is far more useful work for AI agents than one person can set up and watch by hand, and in every area most first ideas do not work. The Agent OS makes trying ideas cheap: many variations of an idea run side by side in a safe test mode, the results show which ones work, and only those are kept. Agents of every kind need the same base (information, running on time, safe testing, getting better, being visible to the owner), so that base is built once and each area adds only what is its own.

Building such a system by vibecoding is fast, but it has a cost. When AI writes most of the plans, docs and code, it soon becomes hard to see what exists, why it exists and what depends on what. A person who cannot see the whole picture cannot steer it, and an AI that cannot see it makes changes that break something somewhere else. So the project is built around two things that keep the picture whole: plain docs at every level, and an IDE that shows every file and folder with an explanation a person can read.

The goals of the project:

- a working Agent OS, built step by step, whose first area is trading on prediction markets;
- an owner who always understands what exists, why, and what is happening, without reading code;
- docs that are exact enough for any AI to act on, so that the next session starts knowing everything the last one learned;
- a project that could be rebuilt by an AI from its docs alone;
- every owner word kept, and every owner question answered where it belongs in the docs.

Success means that the owner can open any part of the project, understand it in one read, ask for a change in plain words, and see that change land everywhere it should, with nothing lost and nothing surprising.

## The concept

The project has two halves that grow together: the system being built, and the way it is built.

**The system.** The Agent OS is made of many small agents, each with one job, grouped by area of work into domains. The system agent looks after the whole system and everything every agent shares. Each domain arranges its agents in the levels its work needs, and every agent has a parent above it. Trading is a group of domains of its own, and its first domain is prediction markets, where agents trade on the outcome of events such as elections or sports. Apps sit beside the agents: tools the project builds for itself, outside tools it uses, and code it only studies.

**The levels of the docs.** The project is described at several levels, from the whole down to its parts. The project level, described here, covers the whole repository and the way of working. Below it come the system level, the level of trading as a whole, the level of all apps, and the level of each app, the project IDE first. Each level has the same set of docs: a vision on top, saying what and why; a README that describes every part of that level exactly and where its own docs are; the same README again in Simplified Technical English (the ASD-STE100 standard), so the two can be compared; and a rebuild prompt, the exact instructions an AI follows to build that level again. A lower level never repeats what a higher level says; it sums it up in a sentence and adds only what is its own.

**Metadata next to everything.** Every file and folder has small companion files beside it: a "How it works" note in plain words, a Details file with the facts about it (who writes it, who reads it, when it changes, what must change with it), and, for the main docs, an outline of their structure and the open questions about them. The project IDE shows each of these as a tab, and shows a tab only when its file really exists.

**The way of working.** The owner vibecodes: they say what they want, in any words and any mix of languages. Every input is kept word for word. Every change gets a written plan first, which the owner sees before anything is built. Then the AI does the work, brings every related doc and note in line, rebuilds the IDE, checks it, and hands the result to the owner, who decides what is merged.

**The project IDE.** The owner's window on the project is the File Tree page: a clickable map of every folder and file in the repository, with its text, its How it works and its other tabs, a box to ask the AI a question or for a change, and a button that carries everything the owner left on the page into the files. The same page runs on claude.ai and on the owner's own server, where Claude Code works behind its request box. The IDE serves every AI too: before it changes a file, an AI sees what the file is for, how it works, what depends on it and which rules reach it from the levels above.

**The planning area.** While the project is planned, one folder holds everything used to plan it: the knowledge base with every input and decision, the plans, the build tools, the page and its server, and the archive of retired texts. It is the workshop; the rest of the repository is the system as designed.

## How it should work

A round of work, from the owner's words to a merged change, goes like this.

1. **The owner says what they want**, in a chat, on the File Tree page, by voice or as an edit to a file. They do not need to know where it belongs.
2. **The input is kept word for word**, with a short summary, its categories and the answer the AI gave. A question and its answer are kept together, because the answer is knowledge too.
3. **A plan comes first** for anything that changes the system, its structure, its code or its docs. The plan says what the owner asked, what will change, which defaults the AI picked and what is still open. The owner reads it and says go, or changes it.
4. **The docs are brought in line, in a fixed order.** At each level touched, the vision first, then the README, then its Simplified Technical English version, then the rebuild prompt last. When a lower level changes, the levels above it are checked too. Decisions and the changelog get their entries.
5. **The metadata follows.** Every How it works note and Details file that the change made stale is rewritten, children before their folders, so a folder always sums up what is inside it.
6. **The IDE is rebuilt and checked.** The page is built again from the repository, tested on a desktop and a phone, and checked so that the tree it shows is exactly the files on disk. A plain list of every path in the repository is written again too.
7. **The work is committed and proposed.** The change goes into the repository with a message that says what changed and why, and into a pull request. It is merged only on the owner's word.

```text
  the owner's words ──► kept word for word ──► plan ──► the owner's go
                                                           │
   merge on the owner's word ◄── commit, pull request ◄── docs, metadata, IDE rebuilt and checked
```

## The business logic

These are the rules the project follows, whatever is being built.

- **Decided means the owner decided.** Anything the AI suggests is a proposal until the owner agrees, and the docs say which is which.
- **Every input is kept.** The owner's words are never changed, never lost and never shortened in the record.
- **Every change has a plan.** Small fixes, such as a typo or a rebuild, need none; everything else is planned and shown first.
- **The docs describe the project as it is now.** No history in the docs for people, no reference numbers and no codes; the history lives in the records.
- **What is learned is written down before the round ends.** Every answer to an owner question is placed in the docs where the owner should have found it.
- **The IDE always shows the real repository.** The tree on the page and the files on disk are the same, every round.
- **Keys never leave the owner's machine.** Only the names of keys are written anywhere; the files that hold their values never go into the repository, and the page never shows them.
- **Nothing hard to undo happens without the owner.** Deleting, rewriting history, merging and anything that acts in the outside world wait for the owner's word.
- **Work is done in stages.** What belongs to a later stage is left as a folder with no files until its stage comes.

The system itself has its own business logic (test first, versions that compete, the owner's approval before anything acts for real), described in the system's vision.

## Examples

**Example: a request from the File Tree page.** The owner opens the How it works of a folder, finds it unclear and writes in the request box: "explain what the jobs file is for, in plain words". The AI answers on the page, keeps the question and the answer as an input, writes the answer into the docs where it belongs, refreshes that How it works note and its folder's, rebuilds the page and commits. The next time anyone opens that folder, the answer is already there.

**Example: a change that touches several levels.** The owner asks that every main doc get a second version of its README in Simplified Technical English. The AI keeps the input, writes a plan with its defaults (the file name, how the page shows it) and waits. After the owner's go, it adds the new skill that writes such a version, writes the new files level by level in the fixed order, adds their How it works and Details files, rebuilds the page so a new tab appears where the file exists, checks that the page tree equals the disk, commits and opens a pull request. The owner reads the result and says merge.

**Example: a session that starts cold.** The owner starts Claude Code on their server in the system's folder. It reads its entry file first, which tells it what the project is, which stage it is in, what to read and in which order, the rules and what to do after every input. Within minutes it knows as much as the session before it, and works by the same rules.

## What the owner sees and does

- They give inputs in plain words: in a chat, by voice, as a note or an edit on the File Tree page.
- They read each plan and say go, or change it.
- They open any file or folder on the page and read what it is, how it works, its details, its outline and its open questions.
- They edit files and How it works notes on the page, add or delete items, and press one button to carry everything into the files.
- They ask questions in the request box and get answers, which are kept.
- They decide what is merged, and answer the open questions when they are ready.

## Where we are and what comes next

The project is in its first stage. The repository already has the shape of the whole system: every planned file and folder exists, written or still empty, each with its metadata files beside it. The File Tree page works on claude.ai and on the owner's server, shows exactly the files on disk, and lets the owner edit, ask, delete and apply changes. The helpers that keep the knowledge and the page, and the skills that write the docs and the metadata, are written as drafts. Research on ways to make money on prediction markets, on agents that improve themselves and on how trading agents are built is in the repository. None of the system's agents is built yet.

Stage one, now:

1. Finish the project IDE, with its own full documentation.
2. Go through every file and folder, write the custom views each kind of item needs, and make all metadata correct.
3. Finish the docs at the project level, the system level, the level of trading as a whole and the level of the apps.

Stage two: the prediction-market domain, its strategies and their trading agents. Until then that domain is only its folders.

Later: building the system's machinery, starting the first strategy chosen by the owner in test mode, more trading domains copied from the first, and agents of other kinds.

## Principles

**The owner understands everything.** If a doc or a note cannot be understood in one read by someone who is not technical, it is not finished.

**One place for each fact.** Each fact lives in the doc that owns it; other docs sum it up, so nothing disagrees.

**Top down, then bottom up.** The vision leads and the other docs follow it; metadata is written from the children up, so a folder always tells the truth about its contents.

**Plain files.** Everything is a file the owner can open; the IDE is built from the files and never holds anything the files do not.

**Plan, then build, then file.** Every change starts as a plan the owner sees, and ends with what it taught placed in the docs.

**Every AI starts with the whole picture.** The docs and the IDE give any session the full context, so changes land everywhere they should.

**Stages keep the work small.** Only the current stage's work is done; later work waits as empty folders, not half-written files.

## Ideas we are still weighing

**One source for every text.** The problem: while the project is planned, some texts exist twice, once in the planning area and once in their place in the repository, and the build copies one over the other. Two copies can drift apart. The idea: make the file in its real place the only source and retire the planning copies, moving the knowledge base, the page and its tools into the IDE's own folders and the helpers into the system's folder. What it would change: one copy of everything, and the planning area left only as an archive.

**A plain file tree that grows.** The plain list of every path is kept without metadata for now. The idea: add a little information to each line later, such as what the item is for. What it would change: a fast overview for people and for AI, at the cost of a longer file to keep current.

## Open questions

- **What should the rebuild doc be called?** It is called the rebuild prompt today; the owner has also called it a reverse prompt. The name appears at every level.
- **Should the repository and its top folder be renamed** to match the name Agent OS? The name appears in links and in every How it works note.
- **What should the front page say?** It is the first thing anyone sees on GitHub, and it is still empty.
- **When does stage two start?** It decides when the first agents are built and when the prediction-market domain gets its files again.

## Going deeper

The README describes every part of the repository exactly: what each part holds, how the parts connect, how a round of work goes, and where each part's own docs are. It is at `docs/README.md`.

# The Agent OS project

## In short

The Agent OS is the owner's personal system for running AI agents of any kind: agents that trade, that work on social media or that help with management. It runs many small agents side by side, each with one clear job, tries every idea safely first and keeps what works. Trading on prediction markets is its first area of work. The owner builds it by vibecoding: they say what they want in plain words, and AI writes the plans, the docs and later the code, while the owner follows and steers everything through the project IDE.

Nothing of the system runs yet. The project is in stage one: finishing the project IDE, making every file's metadata correct, and writing the docs at the project, system, trading and apps levels. The prediction-market domain is stage two.

This document is the full and exact description of the whole repository: every part, what it holds, how the parts connect, how a round of work goes, and where each part's own docs are. Why the project exists, its concept and the rules it follows are in the vision, `docs/vision.md`.

## The repository at a glance

The repository is one GitHub repository, `andyvauliln/trading-oss`. In the docs its top folder is called `agent-os/`, the system's name; the repository keeps its old name for now.

```text
                         the owner
                 (chat, voice, the File Tree page)
                              │ inputs
                              ▼
   vision/  ──── planning area: records, plans, build tools, page source ────┐
      │ build copies drafts and metadata into place                           │ builds
      ▼                                                                       ▼
   agents/            apps/                 docs/            apps/project-IDE/current-ui/
   system/            project-IDE/          (project level)  the File Tree page
   trading/           temp/  trading-ui/                         │
      │                  │                                       │ shows every file
      └──── .secrets/ (key names in git; .env values never) ─────┘ and its metadata
```

| Part | What it is for | Where it lives |
|---|---|---|
| The front page | The first page anyone sees on GitHub | `README.md` |
| The handoff | How to pick the planning work up in a new session | `HANDOFF.md` |
| The project docs | The whole repository and the way it is worked on | `docs/` |
| Agents | Every domain, the system first | `agents/` |
| The system | The system agent, everything every agent shares, and Claude Code's entry point | `agents/system/` |
| Trading | The folder of trading domains, its docs and its research | `agents/trading/` |
| Apps | Our own apps, outside apps we use, research clones | `apps/` |
| The project IDE | The owner's window on the project: the File Tree page, its server, its data | `apps/project-IDE/` |
| Keys | Every private key, kept on the machine | `.secrets/` |
| What git ignores | Keys files, dependencies, caches, editor noise | `.gitignore` |
| Metadata files | How it works, Details and more, next to every file and folder | beside each item |
| The planning area | Everything used to plan the project while it is planned | `vision/` |

How the parts connect, step by step. The owner's words arrive in a chat, by voice or on the File Tree page. The knowledge base agent keeps them word for word in the planning area, writes a plan, and after the owner's go brings the docs of every level touched and their metadata files in line. The project IDE agent then rebuilds the page from the repository: it reads the tree notes and the knowledge from the planning area, copies the drafts and metadata files into their places in the tree, checks that every How it works note is current, and writes the page's data file next to the page. The page shows every file and folder of the repository with its metadata as tabs. What the owner leaves on the page comes back into the files at the next sync. Keys stay in `.secrets/` on the machine; only their names travel.

## How the repository is laid out

The top of the tree:

```text
agent-os/
├── README.md                    the front page for people
├── HANDOFF.md                   how to continue the planning in a new session
├── .gitignore                   what git leaves out: .env files, dependencies, caches
├── .secrets/                    keys: test/.env and live/.env stay on the machine
├── docs/                        the project docs: vision, README, README.asd, rebuild prompt, file tree
├── agents/
│   ├── system/                  the system agent and the shared parts; CLAUDE.md
│   └── trading/                 the folder of trading domains
│       ├── docs/                trading's own docs
│       ├── researches/          the research studies
│       └── prediction-market/   the first trading domain: folders only, stage two
├── apps/
│   ├── docs/                    the docs for all apps
│   ├── project-IDE/             the File Tree page, its server and its data
│   ├── temp/                    repositories cloned only to study them
│   └── trading-ui/              the prediction-market domain's dashboard, empty
└── vision/                      the planning area
```

The levels and where each level's docs are:

```text
project            docs/
├── system         agents/system/docs/
├── trading        agents/trading/docs/
│   └── prediction-market (stage two)   agents/trading/prediction-market/docs/
└── apps           apps/docs/
    └── project IDE                     apps/project-IDE/docs/
```

Every level's docs folder holds the same four docs: `vision.md`, `README.md`, `README.asd.md` and `rebuild-prompt.md`. The project level adds `file-tree.md`, the plain list of every path. A level never repeats its parent; it sums the parent up in a sentence and describes only its own parts.

## The parts

### The front page and the handoff

`README.md` at the top of the repository is the front page GitHub shows. It is meant to say in a few lines what the project is and where to start: the project vision and README in `docs/`. It is still empty; what it says is open.

`HANDOFF.md` is a planning-time file: how to continue the planning in a new Claude Code session, where things stand, the build commands, and the rules to keep. It is written by hand at the end of a planning stretch and read by whoever picks the work up.

Both have their How it works and Details files beside them (`README.index.md`, `README.meta.json`, `HANDOFF.index.md`, `HANDOFF.meta.json`), and the root itself has `agent-os.index.md` and `agent-os.meta.json`.

Its docs: `README.index.md` and `HANDOFF.index.md`.

### The project docs

`docs/` describes the whole repository and the way it is worked on. It is the first thing to read, for people and for every AI session.

- `docs/vision.md`: what the Agent OS project is and why, the way of working, the rules the project follows, examples, the stages and the open questions.
- `docs/README.md`: this document.
- `docs/README.asd.md`: this document again in ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English, with the same content and section order, so the two can be compared. `README.md` is its source.
- `docs/rebuild-prompt.md`: the instructions an AI coding agent follows to build the repository's top level again, then each level in order through that level's own rebuild prompt.
- `docs/file-tree.md`: a plain list of every path in the repository, one per line, with no metadata. It is written by the IDE build every round, never by hand.

Every doc has its How it works and Details files beside it. The four written docs also have `x.example.md`, the outline of the doc (its headings and one line on what goes under each), and `x.questions.md`, the open questions for the owner about it.

The knowledge base agent writes them with its doc skills: `vision-doc`, `readme-doc`, `readme-asd-doc` and `rebuild-prompt-doc`. They change whenever an input changes the project as a whole: its levels, its folders, its way of working, its stage.

Its docs: `docs/docs.index.md`.

### Agents

`agents/` holds every domain, one folder each. The system is a domain too.

Every agent at every level has the same standard folder: `.claude/` (its Claude Code setup: `CLAUDE.md` or its prompt, `settings.json`, `rules/`, `skills/`, `commands/`, `agents/` for its sub-agents, `workflows/`, `output-styles/`, `agent-memory/`), then `configs/`, `scripts/`, `logs/`, `data/`, `docs/`, `tests/`, `research/`, and the level files `package.json`, `requirements.txt`, `init.sh` and `start.sh`. Each content folder holds the level's own files and a `subagents.link/` folder with one link per child agent. What every agent needs lives in the system's folder; what one domain needs lives in that domain. The system README describes all of this exactly.

Its docs: `agents/agents.index.md`.

### The system

`agents/system/` is the system agent's folder: it looks after the whole Agent OS and holds everything every agent shares, whatever its domain.

- `agents/system/CLAUDE.md` is Claude Code's entry point for the whole project. Claude Code started in `agents/system/`, as it is on the owner's server, loads it first. It says what the project is and which stage it is in, what to read and in which order (the project vision and README, the system vision and README, `docs/file-tree.md`, the project IDE's README), the rules, what to do after every input, and when and how each doc is updated. There is no `CLAUDE.md` at the top of the repository.
- `agents/system/.claude/` holds the system's Claude Code setup: `settings.json`, the helper agents in `agents/` (the knowledge base agent, the project IDE agent and the system's self-improvement helper) and the skills in `skills/` (`knowledge-intake`, `change-plan`, `file-index`, `vision-doc`, `readme-doc`, `readme-asd-doc`, `rebuild-prompt-doc`, `claude-md-doc`, `ide-build` with its build scripts in `ide-build/scripts/`, and `ide-sync`; `readme-asd-doc` and `claude-md-doc` are new this stage).
- `agents/system/configs/` holds the system's settings: `system.config.json`, `system.workers.json` (every job the system runs, all switched off for now), `models.config.json` and `system.links.json`.
- `agents/system/docs/` holds the system's four docs.
- `scripts/`, `logs/`, `data/`, `tests/` and `research/` follow the standard folder; most of their files are planned and still empty.

The system level stays general: nothing about money, markets or orders is written there.

Its docs: `agents/system/docs/README.md`.

### Trading

`agents/trading/` is the folder of trading domains. It is not an agent itself: it has no prompt, settings or jobs of its own.

- `agents/trading/docs/` holds trading's four docs: what trading as a whole is for, how its domains relate, and how they are built.
- `agents/trading/researches/` holds the research studies: 42 studies of ways to make money on prediction markets with their evidence and the pipeline that wrote them (`prediction-market-research/`), a study of agents that improve themselves (`self-improving-agents/`), and a study of how trading agents are built (`trding-agents-arhiteches/`).
- `agents/trading/prediction-market/` is the first trading domain. It is stage two: only its folders exist, each empty folder holding a `.gitkeep`, including its first strategy agent `strategy-1-agent/` and that strategy's first trading agent `pm-strategy-1.momentum-v1.opus55-test/`. Its earlier files are kept in the planning area's archive. The build creates nothing inside it until stage two.

The next trading domain, copy trading, will be copied from the prediction-market domain when the owner asks.

Its docs: `agents/trading/docs/README.md`.

### Apps

`apps/` holds applications: our own, outside ones we use, and repositories cloned only to study them. Every app has its own `docs/` with the four docs.

- `apps/docs/` holds the docs for all apps: what apps are for, every app, and where its docs are.
- `apps/project-IDE/` is the owner's IDE, described in the next part.
- `apps/temp/` is for repositories cloned only to study them; each clone sits in its own `repo/` folder, which is never committed. It is empty.
- `apps/trading-ui/` is the planned dashboard of the prediction-market domain. It is empty, and may never be needed if the project IDE does the job.

An outside app we decide to use is forked: our `main` branch holds our changes, and an `upstream` branch follows the source and is merged in from time to time. None is brought in yet.

Its docs: `apps/docs/README.md`.

### The project IDE

`apps/project-IDE/` is the owner's window on the project and the context every AI works from.

- `current-ui/` holds the File Tree page, `file-tree-explorer.html`, and its data file, `file-tree.data.json`. The page is published on claude.ai at https://claude.ai/artifact/72v2Uppt6jpfXLCjKNX9xs.
- `server/` runs the same page on the owner's server, with Claude Code behind its request box: `server.py`, `claude_bridge.py`, `voice.py` (voice input through Groq), `server.config.json` and its own `README.md`.
- `data/` is where the project's records will live: the inputs, decisions, changelog, tree notes, knowledge map, plans, working notes, the page's store and the archive. While we plan, the records are kept in the planning area and the build copies them here.
- `docs/` holds the IDE's four docs; its README is the full documentation of the IDE.

The page shows every file and folder of the repository. A file opens on its File tab, readable or editable; its metadata files show as tabs: How it works, Details, Example, Questions, the ASD-STE100 version of a README, and custom views for some kinds of file, such as the table of key names for a `.env` file. A tab shows only when its file exists. A "metadata" switch shows or hides the metadata files in the tree. Each item has a request box for questions and changes, a voice button on the owner's server, and a Delete button; "Apply changes" at the top carries everything the owner left on the page into the files.

On the owner's server, while we plan, the page is started from the top of the repository with `python3 vision/server/server.py`. It listens only on the machine itself, at `127.0.0.1:8765`, reached through an SSH tunnel.

Its docs: `apps/project-IDE/docs/README.md`.

### Keys and secrets

`.secrets/` at the top of the repository is the one store for every private key, outside `agents/`, so no agent folder or link reaches it.

- `.secrets/test/.env` holds every test key; `.secrets/live/.env` will hold the live keys with the same names, written only by the owner. Both stay on the machine and never go into git.
- `.secrets/secrets.index.json` lists key names and what uses them, never values.
- The folder itself, `test/`, `live/`, the index and every How it works and Details file are in git and show in the tree.

The page lists each `.env` file as local-only and never reads, shows or edits its text. Settings and docs name keys, never their values; today the named keys include `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` for Claude Code on the server and `GROQ_API_KEY` for voice input.

`.gitignore` keeps every `.env` file out of git (except an `.env.example`, which holds names only), while keeping the How it works, Details and Questions files of a keys file. It also leaves out dependencies and build output (`node_modules/`, `dist/`, `build/`, `.venv/`, `venv/`), Python caches, OS and editor files, and Cursor's local state. Each entry carries a comment saying why.

Its docs: `.secrets/.secrets.index.md` and `.gitignore.index.md`.

### Metadata files

Every file and folder outside the planning area has its metadata files beside it. Their names are the item's name without its extension:

| Metadata file | Tab on the page | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| `x.index.md` | How it works | What the item is, who looks after it, when and how it changes, who uses it, where it is mentioned, related knowledge, and up to four "keep in mind" lines, in plain words |
| `x.meta.json` | Details | The facts about the item: what kind it is, its state, whether it is in git or secret, who writes and reads it, when it changes, related files, sources, what must change with it, what applies from above |
| `x.example.md` | Example | The outline of the item: its sections and what goes in each |
| `x.questions.md` | Questions | The open questions for the owner about the item |
| `x.{type}.{name}.view.html` | a custom view | A view for one kind of item; planned |

A folder `f/` keeps its own as `f/f.index.md` and `f/f.meta.json` inside it. A file without an extension keeps its whole name (`.gitignore.index.md`). The root's are `agent-os.index.md` and `agent-os.meta.json`. A metadata file has no metadata files of its own. For now only the main docs and the two `.env` files have Example and Questions files; the `.env` files' example is `.env.example`, with key names only.

While we plan, the source of each How it works and Details file is in the planning area's mirror tree, `vision/tree/agent-os/`, and the build copies it next to its item. The knowledge base agent writes them with the `file-index` skill, children before their folders.

Its docs: `agent-os.index.md` and the `file-index` skill, `agents/system/.claude/skills/file-index/SKILL.md`.

### The planning area

`vision/` holds everything used to plan the project while it is planned. It is the workshop; the rest of the repository is the system as designed.

- `vision/docs/`: the knowledge base. `inputs/` keeps every owner input word for word with its answer (and `index.json`); `decisions.md` keeps every decision; `changelog.md`, newest first; `file-tree.md`, the tree notes, with the planned tree and one section per file and folder; topic notes for agents (`overview.md`, `architecture.md`, `conventions.md`, `safety.md`, `flows.md`, `data-schemas.md`, `glossary.md`, `metrics.md`, `roadmap.md`, `feature-map.md`, `common/`, `how-to/`, `index/` with the knowledge map), and the prediction-market domain's notes in `prediction-market-agents/`.
- `vision/plans/`: one plan per change request, with `index.json`.
- `vision/.claude/`: the planning copies of the helper agents, skills and working memory (`memory/`), and the notes behind each doc (`knowledge/sources/`).
- `vision/tools/`: the build scripts (`parse.py`, `enrich.py`, `materialize.py`, `tabs.py`, `build_map.py`, `index_files.py`, `check_page.js`) and `overrides.json`, the owner's page edits kept in the data.
- `vision/explorer/`: the page source, its data and the texts of the real files it shows.
- `vision/server/`: the page's server, run from here while we plan.
- `vision/tree/agent-os/`: the mirror tree of every How it works and Details file.
- `vision/archive/`: retired texts, by date, among them the earlier drafts of the docs and the prediction-market domain's files, kept for stage two.

The build copies the drafts, records and metadata files from here into their places in the tree. The docs of every level are written in their own folders. Making every real file its own only source, and leaving the planning area as an archive, is still open.

Its docs: `vision/docs/README.md` and `vision/tools/README.md`.

## How a round of work goes

Every round, whether it starts from a chat, the page or the AI's own work, follows the same steps.

1. **Pull.** Bring the latest `main` into the working branch.
2. **File the input.** The knowledge base agent stores the owner's words word for word in `vision/docs/inputs/`, with a summary, categories and the answer, using the `knowledge-intake` skill. A question and its answer are one input.
3. **Plan.** A change to the system, its structure, its code or its docs gets a plan in `vision/plans/` with the `change-plan` skill, shown to the owner. Work starts on the owner's go. Small fixes need no plan.
4. **Update the docs in order.** At each level the change touches: `vision.md`, then `README.md`, then `README.asd.md`, then `rebuild-prompt.md`. Levels in this order: project, system, apps, project IDE, trading. A change at a lower level is carried up to the levels above it. Decisions go into `vision/docs/decisions.md`, a line into `vision/docs/changelog.md`.
5. **Update the metadata.** Every stale How it works and Details file is rewritten with `file-index`, children first, until none is stale.
6. **Rebuild the page.** The project IDE agent runs `ide-build` (with `ide-sync` first when the owner pressed Apply changes): parse, enrich, materialize, check the How it works notes, write `docs/file-tree.md`, test the page and publish it at the same link.
7. **Check the page against the disk.** The page tree must list exactly the files in git (`git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard`), plus the two local-only `.env` files.
8. **Commit** with a message that says what changed and which input caused it.
9. **Open or update a pull request** into `main`.
10. **Merge only on the owner's word.**

## The stages

**Stage one, now.** Finish the project IDE and its full documentation; go through every file and folder, write the custom views, make all metadata correct; finish the docs at the project, system, trading and apps levels. Nothing inside the prediction-market domain is touched.

**Stage two.** The prediction-market domain: its own docs, its strategies and their trading agents. Its earlier files wait in the planning area's archive.

**Later.** The system's machinery, the first strategy in test mode, more trading domains, agents of other kinds.

## Where each part's docs are

| Part | Its docs | What they add |
|---|---|---|
| The whole project | `docs/vision.md`, `docs/README.md` | Why, the way of working, every part of the repository |
| The front page | `README.index.md` | What the front page is for |
| The handoff | `HANDOFF.index.md` | What the handoff is for |
| Every path | `docs/file-tree.md` | The plain list of the repository |
| Claude Code's entry point | `agents/system/CLAUDE.md` | What to read first, the rules, the round |
| Agents | `agents/agents.index.md` | The domains and the standard folder |
| The system | `agents/system/docs/README.md` | Every shared part of the system exactly |
| Trading | `agents/trading/docs/README.md` | The trading domains and their research |
| The prediction-market domain | `agents/trading/prediction-market/docs/` | Stage two; folder only |
| Apps | `apps/docs/README.md` | Every app and how apps are brought in |
| The project IDE | `apps/project-IDE/docs/README.md` | The full documentation of the IDE |
| The IDE server | `apps/project-IDE/server/README.md` | How to run the page on the owner's server |
| Keys | `.secrets/.secrets.index.md` | How keys are kept |
| What git ignores | `.gitignore.index.md` | Each ignore rule |
| Metadata files | `agent-os.index.md`, `agents/system/.claude/skills/file-index/SKILL.md` | How every How it works file is written |
| The planning area | `vision/docs/README.md`, `vision/tools/README.md` | The knowledge base and the build |

## Still open in the design

- **Doc names:** whether `rebuild-prompt.md` keeps its name or becomes `reverse-prompt.md`.
- **Repository name:** whether the repository and its top folder are renamed to `agent-os`.
- **Front page:** what `README.md` at the top says; it is empty.
- **Planning area:** when the real files become the only source and `vision/` becomes an archive; until then the build copies drafts over their places.
- **Records:** whether the records move from `vision/docs/` into `apps/project-IDE/data/` as planned.
- **The plain file tree:** whether `docs/file-tree.md` later gets a little information on each line.
- **Metadata tabs:** which other files get Example, Questions, Tests and changelog files, and which custom views each kind of item gets.
- **Prediction-market folder names:** whether its strategy and trading agent folders keep their current names.

# Open questions: docs/README.md

- **Should the records (inputs, decisions, changelog, tree notes, plans) move from `vision/docs/` into `apps/project-IDE/data/`?** The README describes both places; it decides which one is the source.
- **Should `docs/file-tree.md` list the metadata files too, or only the items?** Listing every `.index.md` and `.meta.json` roughly doubles the file; leaving them out makes it a cleaner map.
- **Should the logs and data of agents be ignored by git again?** The current `.gitignore` no longer has the rules that keep runtime `logs/` and `data/` and research clones in `apps/temp/` out of git, which the owner asked for earlier.
- **Is `HANDOFF.md` still needed once `agents/system/CLAUDE.md` is the entry point?** Both tell a new session where to start, and two starting points can disagree.

This is the ASD-STE100 version of `docs/README.md`. `README.md` is the source. If the two documents are different, `README.md` is correct.

# The Agent OS project

## In short

The Agent OS is a personal system of the owner. It operates AI agents of different kinds. Examples are agents that trade, agents that work on social media and agents that help with management.

The system operates many small agents at the same time. Each agent has one clear task. The system tests each idea safely first. It keeps the ideas that work. The first area of work is trading on prediction markets.

The owner builds the system by vibecoding. The owner tells the AI what to do in plain words. The AI writes the plans, the docs and, later, the code. The owner monitors and controls all the work through the project IDE.

The system does not operate yet. The project is in stage one. In stage one, we complete the project IDE and we make all metadata correct. We also write the docs of the project, the system, trading and the apps. The prediction-market domain is in stage two.

This document gives a full and exact description of the repository. It tells each part, the contents of each part and the connections between the parts. It tells the steps of a round of work. It gives the location of the docs of each part. The vision, `docs/vision.md`, tells why the project exists, its concept and its rules.

## The repository at a glance

The project is one GitHub repository, `andyvauliln/trading-oss`. The docs use the name `agent-os/` for the top folder. The repository keeps its old name for now.

```text
                         the owner
                 (chat, voice, the File Tree page)
                              │ inputs
                              ▼
   vision/  ──── planning area: records, plans, build tools, page source ────┐
      │ build copies drafts and metadata into place                           │ builds
      ▼                                                                       ▼
   agents/            apps/                 docs/            apps/project-IDE/current-ui/
   system/            project-IDE/          (project level)  the File Tree page
   trading/           temp/  trading-ui/                         │
      │                  │                                       │ shows every file
      └──── .secrets/ (key names in git; .env values never) ─────┘ and its metadata
```

| Part | Purpose | Location |
|---|---|---|
| The front page | The first page that GitHub shows | `README.md` |
| The handoff | It tells how to continue the planning in a new session | `HANDOFF.md` |
| The project docs | They describe the full repository and the method of work | `docs/` |
| Agents | All domains. The system is the first domain | `agents/` |
| The system | The system agent, the shared parts and the entry point for Claude Code | `agents/system/` |
| Trading | The folder of trading domains, with its docs and its research | `agents/trading/` |
| Apps | Our apps, outside apps that we use, and research clones | `apps/` |
| The project IDE | The File Tree page, its server and its data | `apps/project-IDE/` |
| Keys | All private keys. The keys stay on the machine | `.secrets/` |
| Git ignore rules | Keys files, dependencies, caches and editor files | `.gitignore` |
| Metadata files | How it works, Details and other files for each item | Next to each item |
| The planning area | All the material that we use to plan the project | `vision/` |

The parts connect in these steps:

1. The owner gives an input in a chat, by voice or on the File Tree page.
2. The knowledge base agent keeps the input word for word in the planning area.
3. The knowledge base agent writes a plan.
4. The owner approves the plan. Then the knowledge base agent updates the docs and metadata files of each level that the change touches.
5. The project IDE agent builds the page again from the repository.
6. The build reads the tree notes and the knowledge in the planning area.
7. The build copies the drafts and the metadata files to their locations in the tree.
8. The build makes sure that each How it works file is current.
9. The build writes the data file of the page next to the page.
10. The page shows each file and each folder of the repository. It shows the metadata of each item as tabs.
11. At the next sync, the AI puts the changes from the page into the files.

The keys stay in `.secrets/` on the machine. Only the names of the keys go to other files.

## How the repository is laid out

This is the top of the tree:

```text
agent-os/
├── README.md                    the front page for people
├── HANDOFF.md                   how to continue the planning in a new session
├── .gitignore                   what git leaves out: .env files, dependencies, caches
├── .secrets/                    keys: test/.env and live/.env stay on the machine
├── docs/                        the project docs: vision, README, README.asd, rebuild prompt, file tree
├── agents/
│   ├── system/                  the system agent and the shared parts; CLAUDE.md
│   └── trading/                 the folder of trading domains
│       ├── docs/                trading's own docs
│       ├── researches/          the research studies
│       └── prediction-market/   the first trading domain: folders only, stage two
├── apps/
│   ├── docs/                    the docs for all apps
│   ├── project-IDE/             the File Tree page, its server and its data
│   ├── temp/                    repositories cloned only to study them
│   └── trading-ui/              the prediction-market domain's dashboard, empty
└── vision/                      the planning area
```

These are the levels and the location of the docs of each level:

```text
project            docs/
├── system         agents/system/docs/
├── trading        agents/trading/docs/
│   └── prediction-market (stage two)   agents/trading/prediction-market/docs/
└── apps           apps/docs/
    └── project IDE                     apps/project-IDE/docs/
```

The docs folder of each level has the same four docs: `vision.md`, `README.md`, `README.asd.md` and `rebuild-prompt.md`. The project level also has `file-tree.md`. This file is a plain list of all paths.

A level does not repeat the text of its parent level. It gives a short summary of the parent level in one or two sentences. Then it describes only its own parts.

## The parts

### The front page and the handoff

`README.md` at the top of the repository is the front page that GitHub shows. It must tell in a few lines what the project is. It must tell where to start: the project vision and the project README in `docs/`. The front page is empty now. Its content is an open subject.

`HANDOFF.md` is a file for the planning time. It tells how to continue the planning in a new Claude Code session. It tells the current status, the build commands and the rules. A person writes it at the end of a period of planning. The next person or AI reads it.

Each of these two files has its How it works file and its Details file next to it: `README.index.md`, `README.meta.json`, `HANDOFF.index.md` and `HANDOFF.meta.json`. The root has `agent-os.index.md` and `agent-os.meta.json`.

Its docs: `README.index.md` and `HANDOFF.index.md`.

### The project docs

`docs/` describes the full repository and the method of work. People and AI sessions read it first.

- `docs/vision.md` tells what the project is and why. It tells the method of work, the rules, examples, the stages and the open questions.
- `docs/README.md` is the source of this document.
- `docs/README.asd.md` is this document. It has the same content and the same section order as `README.md`. It uses ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English. The owner can compare the two documents.
- `docs/rebuild-prompt.md` gives the instructions to an AI coding agent. With these instructions, the agent builds the top level of the repository again. Then it builds each level with the rebuild prompt of that level.
- `docs/file-tree.md` is a plain list of all paths in the repository, one path on each line. It has no metadata. The IDE build writes it in each round. Do not write it by hand.

Each doc has its How it works file and its Details file next to it. The four written docs also have two more files:

- `x.example.md` gives the outline of the doc: the headings and one line about the content of each heading.
- `x.questions.md` gives the open questions for the owner about the doc.

The knowledge base agent writes these docs with its doc skills: `vision-doc`, `readme-doc`, `readme-asd-doc` and `rebuild-prompt-doc`. The docs change when an input changes the full project. Examples are a change to the levels, the folders, the method of work or the stage.

Its docs: `docs/docs.index.md`.

### Agents

`agents/` contains all domains, one folder for each domain. The system is also a domain.

Each agent at each level has the same standard folder. The standard folder contains:

- `.claude/`, the Claude Code setup of the agent. It contains `CLAUDE.md` or the prompt, `settings.json`, `rules/`, `skills/`, `commands/`, `agents/` for sub-agents, `workflows/`, `output-styles/` and `agent-memory/`.
- `configs/`, `scripts/`, `logs/`, `data/`, `docs/`, `tests/` and `research/`.
- The level files `package.json`, `requirements.txt`, `init.sh` and `start.sh`.

Each content folder contains the files of its own level. It also contains a `subagents.link/` folder with one link for each child agent. The files that all agents need are in the folder of the system. The files that one domain needs are in that domain. The system README gives the exact description.

Its docs: `agents/agents.index.md`.

### The system

`agents/system/` is the folder of the system agent. The system agent manages the full Agent OS. The folder contains all parts that all agents share, in all domains.

- `agents/system/CLAUDE.md` is the entry point for Claude Code for the full project. When Claude Code starts in `agents/system/`, it reads this file first. Claude Code starts there on the owner's server.
- `CLAUDE.md` tells what the project is and its current stage.
- `CLAUDE.md` tells which files to read and in which order. The order is: the project vision and README, the system vision and README, `docs/file-tree.md` and the README of the project IDE.
- `CLAUDE.md` also gives the rules, the steps after each input, and when and how to update each doc.
- There is no `CLAUDE.md` at the top of the repository.
- `agents/system/.claude/` contains the Claude Code setup of the system: `settings.json`, the helper agents in `agents/` and the skills in `skills/`.
- The helper agents are the knowledge base agent, the project IDE agent and the self-improvement helper of the system.
- The skills are `knowledge-intake`, `change-plan`, `file-index`, `vision-doc`, `readme-doc`, `readme-asd-doc`, `rebuild-prompt-doc`, `claude-md-doc`, `ide-build` and `ide-sync`. The skills `readme-asd-doc` and `claude-md-doc` are new in this stage. The build scripts are in `ide-build/scripts/`.
- `agents/system/configs/` contains the settings of the system: `system.config.json`, `system.workers.json`, `models.config.json` and `system.links.json`. `system.workers.json` lists all jobs of the system. All jobs are off now.
- `agents/system/docs/` contains the four docs of the system.
- `scripts/`, `logs/`, `data/`, `tests/` and `research/` follow the standard folder. Most of their files are planned and empty.

The system level is general. Do not write about money, markets or orders at the system level.

Its docs: `agents/system/docs/README.md`.

### Trading

`agents/trading/` is the folder of trading domains. It is not an agent. It has no prompt, no settings and no jobs.

- `agents/trading/docs/` contains the four docs of trading. They tell the purpose of trading, the relation between the trading domains and how to build them.
- `agents/trading/researches/` contains the research studies.
- `prediction-market-research/` contains 42 studies about methods to make money on prediction markets. It also contains their evidence and the pipeline that wrote them.
- `self-improving-agents/` contains a study about agents that improve themselves.
- `trding-agents-arhiteches/` contains a study about the structure of trading agents.
- `agents/trading/prediction-market/` is the first trading domain. It is in stage two.
- In the prediction-market domain, only the folders exist. Each empty folder contains a `.gitkeep` file.
- The folders include the first strategy agent `strategy-1-agent/` and its first trading agent `pm-strategy-1.momentum-v1.opus55-test/`.
- The old files of the domain are in the archive of the planning area. The build does not make files in the domain until stage two.

The next trading domain is copy trading. We make it as a copy of the prediction-market domain when the owner asks.

Its docs: `agents/trading/docs/README.md`.

### Apps

`apps/` contains applications. These are our own apps, outside apps that we use, and repositories that we clone only for study. Each app has its own `docs/` folder with the four docs.

- `apps/docs/` contains the docs for all apps. They tell the purpose of apps, each app and the location of its docs.
- `apps/project-IDE/` is the IDE of the owner. The next part describes it.
- `apps/temp/` is for repositories that we clone only for study. Each clone is in its own `repo/` folder. Do not put a clone in git. The folder is empty now.
- `apps/trading-ui/` is the planned dashboard of the prediction-market domain. It is empty. Possibly it is not necessary, because the project IDE can do its work.

When we use an outside app, we fork it. Our `main` branch contains our changes. An `upstream` branch follows the source. From time to time, we merge `upstream` into `main`. We do not use an outside app yet.

Its docs: `apps/docs/README.md`.

### The project IDE

`apps/project-IDE/` is the window of the owner on the project. It also gives the context to each AI.

- `current-ui/` contains the File Tree page, `file-tree-explorer.html`, and its data file, `file-tree.data.json`. The page is on claude.ai at https://claude.ai/artifact/72v2Uppt6jpfXLCjKNX9xs.
- `server/` operates the same page on the owner's server. Claude Code operates behind the request box of the page.
- The server files are `server.py`, `claude_bridge.py`, `voice.py`, `server.config.json` and `README.md`. `voice.py` changes speech to text with Groq.
- `data/` is the planned location of the project records: inputs, decisions, changelog, tree notes, knowledge map, plans, working notes, the page store and the archive.
- During the planning, the records are in the planning area. The build copies them into `data/`.
- `docs/` contains the four docs of the IDE. Its README is the full documentation of the IDE.

The page shows each file and each folder of the repository:

- The File tab shows the text of a file. The owner can read and edit the text.
- The metadata files show as tabs: How it works, Details, Example, Questions and the ASD-STE100 version of a README.
- Some kinds of file have custom views. An example is the table of key names for a `.env` file.
- A tab shows only when its file exists.
- A "metadata" switch shows or hides the metadata files in the tree.
- Each item has a request box for questions and changes.
- On the owner's server, a voice button records the owner.
- Each item has a Delete button.
- The "Apply changes" button at the top puts all changes from the page into the files.

During the planning, start the page on the owner's server from the top of the repository with `python3 vision/server/server.py`. The server listens only on the machine, at `127.0.0.1:8765`. Use an SSH tunnel to open it.

Its docs: `apps/project-IDE/docs/README.md`.

### Keys and secrets

`.secrets/` at the top of the repository is the one location for all private keys. It is outside `agents/`. Thus no agent folder and no link can get to it.

- `.secrets/test/.env` contains all test keys.
- `.secrets/live/.env` will contain the live keys, with the same names. Only the owner writes this file.
- The two `.env` files stay on the machine. Do not put them in git.
- `.secrets/secrets.index.json` lists the key names and the files that use them. It does not contain values.
- The folder, `test/`, `live/`, the index and all How it works and Details files are in git. They show in the tree.

The page shows each `.env` file as local-only. The page does not read, show or edit the text of a `.env` file.

Settings and docs give the names of keys. They do not give the values. Two of the key names are `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, for Claude Code on the server, and `GROQ_API_KEY`, for voice input.

`.gitignore` keeps all `.env` files out of git. An `.env.example` file is the exception, because it contains only names. `.gitignore` keeps the How it works, Details and Questions files of a keys file in git. It also keeps these items out of git:

- dependencies and build output: `node_modules/`, `dist/`, `build/`, `.venv/` and `venv/`
- Python caches
- OS files and editor files
- the local state of Cursor

Each entry in `.gitignore` has a comment that tells why.

Its docs: `.secrets/.secrets.index.md` and `.gitignore.index.md`.

### Metadata files

Each file and each folder outside the planning area has metadata files next to it. The name of a metadata file is the name of the item without its extension.

| Metadata file | Tab on the page | Content |
|---|---|---|
| `x.index.md` | How it works | What the item is, who keeps it, when and how it changes, who uses it, where other files mention it, related knowledge, and a maximum of four "keep in mind" lines, in plain words |
| `x.meta.json` | Details | The facts about the item: its kind, its state, git or secret, who writes it, who reads it, when it changes, related files, sources, what must change with it, and what applies from the levels above |
| `x.example.md` | Example | The outline of the item: its sections and the content of each section |
| `x.questions.md` | Questions | The open questions for the owner about the item |
| `x.{type}.{name}.view.html` | A custom view | A view for one kind of item. It is planned |

- A folder `f/` keeps its metadata files inside it, as `f/f.index.md` and `f/f.meta.json`.
- A file without an extension keeps its full name, for example `.gitignore.index.md`.
- The metadata files of the root are `agent-os.index.md` and `agent-os.meta.json`.
- A metadata file has no metadata files.
- Now, only the main docs and the two `.env` files have Example files and Questions files. The example of a `.env` file is `.env.example`. It contains only key names.

During the planning, the source of each How it works file and each Details file is in the mirror tree of the planning area, `vision/tree/agent-os/`. The build copies each file next to its item. The knowledge base agent writes these files with the `file-index` skill. It writes the children before their folders.

Its docs: `agent-os.index.md` and the `file-index` skill, `agents/system/.claude/skills/file-index/SKILL.md`.

### The planning area

`vision/` contains all the material that we use to plan the project. It is the workshop. The other parts of the repository are the system as we design it.

- `vision/docs/` is the knowledge base.
- `vision/docs/inputs/` keeps each owner input word for word, with its answer. It also has `index.json`.
- `vision/docs/decisions.md` keeps all decisions.
- `vision/docs/changelog.md` records the changes. The newest change is first.
- `vision/docs/file-tree.md` contains the tree notes: the planned tree and one section for each file and each folder.
- `vision/docs/` also contains topic notes for agents: `overview.md`, `architecture.md`, `conventions.md`, `safety.md`, `flows.md`, `data-schemas.md`, `glossary.md`, `metrics.md`, `roadmap.md`, `feature-map.md`, `common/`, `how-to/` and `index/`. `index/` contains the knowledge map.
- `vision/docs/prediction-market-agents/` contains the notes of the prediction-market domain.
- `vision/plans/` contains one plan for each change request, and `index.json`.
- `vision/.claude/` contains the planning copies of the helper agents, the skills and the working memory (`memory/`). It also contains the notes behind each doc (`knowledge/sources/`).
- `vision/tools/` contains the build scripts: `parse.py`, `enrich.py`, `materialize.py`, `tabs.py`, `build_map.py`, `index_files.py` and `check_page.js`. It also contains `overrides.json`, which keeps the owner's page edits in the data.
- `vision/explorer/` contains the page source, its data and the texts of the real files that the page shows.
- `vision/server/` contains the server of the page. During the planning, the server operates from here.
- `vision/tree/agent-os/` is the mirror tree of all How it works files and Details files.
- `vision/archive/` keeps old texts, by date. It includes the old drafts of the docs and the files of the prediction-market domain for stage two.

The build copies the drafts, records and metadata files from `vision/` to their locations in the tree. We write the docs of each level in their own folders.

It is an open subject when the real files become the only source. After that change, `vision/` becomes an archive.

Its docs: `vision/docs/README.md` and `vision/tools/README.md`.

## How a round of work goes

Each round has the same steps. The source of the round can be a chat, the page or the work of the AI.

1. Pull the latest `main` into the working branch.
2. Keep the owner's input word for word in `vision/docs/inputs/`. Use the `knowledge-intake` skill. Add a summary, the categories and the answer. Keep a question and its answer as one input.
3. Write a plan in `vision/plans/` with the `change-plan` skill. Show the plan to the owner. Start the work only after the owner approves it. A small fix does not need a plan.
4. Update the docs of each level that the change touches. Use this order in each level: `vision.md`, `README.md`, `README.asd.md`, `rebuild-prompt.md`.
5. Use this order of levels: project, system, apps, project IDE, trading. When a lower level changes, update the levels above it.
6. Write the decisions in `vision/docs/decisions.md`. Write a line in `vision/docs/changelog.md`.
7. Write each stale How it works file and Details file again with `file-index`. Do the children first. Continue until no file is stale.
8. Build the page again with `ide-build`. If the owner pushed "Apply changes", do `ide-sync` first.
9. The build does these steps: parse, enrich, materialize, check the How it works files, write `docs/file-tree.md`, test the page and publish it at the same link.
10. Compare the page tree with the disk. The page tree must list the same files as git (`git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard`), and the two local-only `.env` files.
11. Commit the change. The message must tell what changed and which input caused the change.
12. Open or update a pull request into `main`.
13. Merge only when the owner tells you to merge.

## The stages

Stage one is the current stage. In stage one, we do this work:

1. Complete the project IDE and its full documentation.
2. Examine each file and each folder. Write the custom views. Make all metadata correct.
3. Complete the docs of the project, the system, trading and the apps.

In stage one, do not change the contents of the prediction-market domain.

Stage two is the prediction-market domain: its docs, its strategies and their trading agents. The old files of the domain wait in the archive of the planning area.

After stage two, we build the machinery of the system. We start the first strategy in test mode. We add more trading domains and agents of other kinds.

## Where each part's docs are

| Part | Its docs | Content |
|---|---|---|
| The full project | `docs/vision.md`, `docs/README.md` | Why, the method of work and each part of the repository |
| The front page | `README.index.md` | The purpose of the front page |
| The handoff | `HANDOFF.index.md` | The purpose of the handoff |
| All paths | `docs/file-tree.md` | The plain list of the repository |
| The entry point for Claude Code | `agents/system/CLAUDE.md` | What to read first, the rules and the round |
| Agents | `agents/agents.index.md` | The domains and the standard folder |
| The system | `agents/system/docs/README.md` | The exact description of each shared part of the system |
| Trading | `agents/trading/docs/README.md` | The trading domains and their research |
| The prediction-market domain | `agents/trading/prediction-market/docs/` | Stage two. Only the folder exists |
| Apps | `apps/docs/README.md` | Each app and how we add apps |
| The project IDE | `apps/project-IDE/docs/README.md` | The full documentation of the IDE |
| The IDE server | `apps/project-IDE/server/README.md` | How to operate the page on the owner's server |
| Keys | `.secrets/.secrets.index.md` | How we keep keys |
| Git ignore rules | `.gitignore.index.md` | Each ignore rule |
| Metadata files | `agent-os.index.md`, `agents/system/.claude/skills/file-index/SKILL.md` | How to write each How it works file |
| The planning area | `vision/docs/README.md`, `vision/tools/README.md` | The knowledge base and the build |

## Still open in the design

- Doc names: Do we keep the name `rebuild-prompt.md`, or do we change it to `reverse-prompt.md`?
- Repository name: Do we change the name of the repository and its top folder to `agent-os`?
- Front page: What does `README.md` at the top tell? It is empty now.
- Planning area: When do the real files become the only source? When does `vision/` become an archive? Until then, the build copies the drafts to their locations.
- Records: Do the records move from `vision/docs/` to `apps/project-IDE/data/`, as planned?
- Plain file tree: Do we add some information to each line of `docs/file-tree.md` later?
- Metadata tabs: Which other files get Example, Questions, Tests and changelog files? Which custom views does each kind of item get?
- Folder names in the prediction-market domain: Do the strategy folders and the trading agent folders keep their current names?
