nodes.content:
This is the ASD-STE100 version of `docs/README.md`. `README.md` is the source. If the two documents are different, `README.md` is correct.

# The Agent OS project

## In short

The Agent OS is a personal system of the owner. It operates AI agents of different kinds. Examples are agents that trade, agents that work on social media and agents that help with management.

The system operates many small agents at the same time. Each agent has one clear task. The system tests each idea safely first. It keeps the ideas that work. The first area of work is trading on prediction markets.

The owner builds the system by vibecoding. The owner tells the AI what to do in plain words. The AI writes the plans, the docs and, later, the code. The owner monitors and controls all the work through the project IDE.

The system does not operate yet. The project is in stage one. In stage one, we complete the project IDE and we make all metadata correct. We also write the docs of the project, the system, trading and the apps. The prediction-market domain is in stage two.

This document gives a full and exact description of the repository. It tells each part, the contents of each part and the connections between the parts. It tells the steps of a round of work. It gives the location of the docs of each part. The vision, `docs/vision.md`, tells why the project exists, its concept and its rules.

## The repository at a glance

The project is one GitHub repository, `andyvauliln/trading-oss`. The docs use the name `agent-os/` for the top folder. The repository keeps its old name for now.

```text
                         the owner
                 (chat, voice, the File Tree page)
                              │ inputs
                              ▼
   vision/  ──── planning area: records, plans, build tools, page source ────┐
      │ build copies drafts and metadata into place                           │ builds
      ▼                                                                       ▼
   agents/            apps/                 docs/            apps/project-IDE/current-ui/
   system/            project-IDE/          (project level)  the File Tree page
   trading/           temp/  trading-ui/                         │
      │                  │                                       │ shows every file
      └──── .secrets/ (key names in git; .env values never) ─────┘ and its metadata
```

| Part | Purpose | Location |
|---|---|---|
| The front page | The first page that GitHub shows | `README.md` |
| The handoff | It tells how to continue the planning in a new session | `HANDOFF.md` |
| The project docs | They describe the full repository and the method of work | `docs/` |
| Agents | All domains. The system is the first domain | `agents/` |
| The system | The system agent, the shared parts and the entry point for Claude Code | `agents/system/` |
| Trading | The folder of trading domains, with its docs and its research | `agents/trading/` |
| Apps | Our apps, outside apps that we use, and research clones | `apps/` |
| The project IDE | The File Tree page, its server and its data | `apps/project-IDE/` |
| Keys | All private keys. The keys stay on the machine | `.secrets/` |
| Git ignore rules | Keys files, dependencies, caches and editor files | `.gitignore` |
| Metadata files | How it works, Details and other files for each item | Next to each item |
| The planning area | All the material that we use to plan the project | `vision/` |

The parts connect in these steps:

1. The owner gives an input in a chat, by voice or on the File Tree page.
2. The knowledge base agent keeps the input word for word in the planning area.
3. The knowledge base agent writes a plan.
4. The owner approves the plan. Then the knowledge base agent updates the docs and metadata files of each level that the change touches.
5. The project IDE agent builds the page again from the repository.
6. The build reads the tree notes and the knowledge in the planning area.
7. The build copies the drafts and the metadata files to their locations in the tree.
8. The build makes sure that each How it works file is current.
9. The build writes the data file of the page next to the page.
10. The page shows each file and each folder of the repository. It shows the metadata of each item as tabs.
11. At the next sync, the AI puts the changes from the page into the files.

The keys stay in `.secrets/` on the machine. Only the names of the keys go to other files.

## How the repository is laid out

This is the top of the tree:

```text
agent-os/
├── README.md                    the front page for people
├── HANDOFF.md                   how to continue the planning in a new session
├── .gitignore                   what git leaves out: .env files, dependencies, caches
├── .secrets/                    keys: test/.env and live/.env stay on the machine
├── docs/                        the project docs: vision, README, README.asd, rebuild prompt, file tree
├── agents/
│   ├── system/                  the system agent and the shared parts; CLAUDE.md
│   └── trading/                 the folder of trading domains
│       ├── docs/                trading's own docs
│       ├── researches/          the research studies
│       └── prediction-market/   the first trading domain: folders only, stage two
├── apps/
│   ├── docs/                    the docs for all apps
│   ├── project-IDE/             the File Tree page, its server and its data
│   ├── temp/                    repositories cloned only to study them
│   └── trading-ui/              the prediction-market domain's dashboard, empty
└── vision/                      the planning area
```

These are the levels and the location of the docs of each level:

```text
project            docs/
├── system         agents/system/docs/
├── trading        agents/trading/docs/
│   └── prediction-market (stage two)   agents/trading/prediction-market/docs/
└── apps           apps/docs/
    └── project IDE                     apps/project-IDE/docs/
```

The docs folder of each level has the same four docs: `vision.md`, `README.md`, `README.asd.md` and `rebuild-prompt.md`. The project level also has `file-tree.md`. This file is a plain list of all paths.

A level does not repeat the text of its parent level. It gives a short summary of the parent level in one or two sentences. Then it describes only its own parts.

## The parts

### The front page and the handoff

`README.md` at the top of the repository is the front page that GitHub shows. It must tell in a few lines what the project is. It must tell where to start: the project vision and the project README in `docs/`. The front page is empty now. Its content is an open subject.

`HANDOFF.md` is a file for the planning time. It tells how to continue the planning in a new Claude Code session. It tells the current status, the build commands and the rules. A person writes it at the end of a period of planning. The next person or AI reads it.

Each of these two files has its How it works file and its Details file next to it: `README.index.md`, `README.meta.json`, `HANDOFF.index.md` and `HANDOFF.meta.json`. The root has `agent-os.index.md` and `agent-os.meta.json`.

Its docs: `README.index.md` and `HANDOFF.index.md`.

### The project docs

`docs/` describes the full repository and the method of work. People and AI sessions read it first.

- `docs/vision.md` tells what the project is and why. It tells the method of work, the rules, examples, the stages and the open questions.
- `docs/README.md` is the source of this document.
- `docs/README.asd.md` is this document. It has the same content and the same section order as `README.md`. It uses ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English. The owner can compare the two documents.
- `docs/rebuild-prompt.md` gives the instructions to an AI coding agent. With these instructions, the agent builds the top level of the repository again. Then it builds each level with the rebuild prompt of that level.
- `docs/file-tree.md` is a plain list of all paths in the repository, one path on each line. It has no metadata. The IDE build writes it in each round. Do not write it by hand.

Each doc has its How it works file and its Details file next to it. The four written docs also have two more files:

- `x.example.md` gives the outline of the doc: the headings and one line about the content of each heading.
- `x.questions.md` gives the open questions for the owner about the doc.

The knowledge base agent writes these docs with its doc skills: `vision-doc`, `readme-doc`, `readme-asd-doc` and `rebuild-prompt-doc`. The docs change when an input changes the full project. Examples are a change to the levels, the folders, the method of work or the stage.

Its docs: `docs/docs.index.md`.

### Agents

`agents/` contains all domains, one folder for each domain. The system is also a domain.

Each agent at each level has the same standard folder. The standard folder contains:

- `.claude/`, the Claude Code setup of the agent. It contains `CLAUDE.md` or the prompt, `settings.json`, `rules/`, `skills/`, `commands/`, `agents/` for sub-agents, `workflows/`, `output-styles/` and `agent-memory/`.
- `configs/`, `scripts/`, `logs/`, `data/`, `docs/`, `tests/` and `research/`.
- The level files `package.json`, `requirements.txt`, `init.sh` and `start.sh`.

Each content folder contains the files of its own level. It also contains a `subagents.link/` folder with one link for each child agent. The files that all agents need are in the folder of the system. The files that one domain needs are in that domain. The system README gives the exact description.

Its docs: `agents/agents.index.md`.

### The system

`agents/system/` is the folder of the system agent. The system agent manages the full Agent OS. The folder contains all parts that all agents share, in all domains.

- `agents/system/CLAUDE.md` is the entry point for Claude Code for the full project. When Claude Code starts in `agents/system/`, it reads this file first. Claude Code starts there on the owner's server.
- `CLAUDE.md` tells what the project is and its current stage.
- `CLAUDE.md` tells which files to read and in which order. The order is: the project vision and README, the system vision and README, `docs/file-tree.md` and the README of the project IDE.
- `CLAUDE.md` also gives the rules, the steps after each input, and when and how to update each doc.
- There is no `CLAUDE.md` at the top of the repository.
- `agents/system/.claude/` contains the Claude Code setup of the system: `settings.json`, the helper agents in `agents/` and the skills in `skills/`.
- The helper agents are the knowledge base agent, the project IDE agent and the self-improvement helper of the system.
- The skills are `knowledge-intake`, `change-plan`, `file-index`, `vision-doc`, `readme-doc`, `readme-asd-doc`, `rebuild-prompt-doc`, `claude-md-doc`, `ide-build` and `ide-sync`. The skills `readme-asd-doc` and `claude-md-doc` are new in this stage. The build scripts are in `ide-build/scripts/`.
- `agents/system/configs/` contains the settings of the system: `system.config.json`, `system.workers.json`, `models.config.json` and `system.links.json`. `system.workers.json` lists all jobs of the system. All jobs are off now.
- `agents/system/docs/` contains the four docs of the system.
- `scripts/`, `logs/`, `data/`, `tests/` and `research/` follow the standard folder. Most of their files are planned and empty.

The system level is general. Do not write about money, markets or orders at the system level.

Its docs: `agents/system/docs/README.md`.

### Trading

`agents/trading/` is the folder of trading domains. It is not an agent. It has no prompt, no settings and no jobs.

- `agents/trading/docs/` contains the four docs of trading. They tell the purpose of trading, the relation between the trading domains and how to build them.
- `agents/trading/researches/` contains the research studies.
- `prediction-market-research/` contains 42 studies about methods to make money on prediction markets. It also contains their evidence and the pipeline that wrote them.
- `self-improving-agents/` contains a study about agents that improve themselves.
- `trding-agents-arhiteches/` contains a study about the structure of trading agents.
- `agents/trading/prediction-market/` is the first trading domain. It is in stage two.
- In the prediction-market domain, only the folders exist. Each empty folder contains a `.gitkeep` file.
- The folders include the first strategy agent `strategy-1-agent/` and its first trading agent `pm-strategy-1.momentum-v1.opus55-test/`.
- The old files of the domain are in the archive of the planning area. The build does not make files in the domain until stage two.

The next trading domain is copy trading. We make it as a copy of the prediction-market domain when the owner asks.

Its docs: `agents/trading/docs/README.md`.

### Apps

`apps/` contains applications. These are our own apps, outside apps that we use, and repositories that we clone only for study. Each app has its own `docs/` folder with the four docs.

- `apps/docs/` contains the docs for all apps. They tell the purpose of apps, each app and the location of its docs.
- `apps/project-IDE/` is the IDE of the owner. The next part describes it.
- `apps/temp/` is for repositories that we clone only for study. Each clone is in its own `repo/` folder. Do not put a clone in git. The folder is empty now.
- `apps/trading-ui/` is the planned dashboard of the prediction-market domain. It is empty. Possibly it is not necessary, because the project IDE can do its work.

When we use an outside app, we fork it. Our `main` branch contains our changes. An `upstream` branch follows the source. From time to time, we merge `upstream` into `main`. We do not use an outside app yet.

Its docs: `apps/docs/README.md`.

### The project IDE

`apps/project-IDE/` is the window of the owner on the project. It also gives the context to each AI.

- `current-ui/` contains the File Tree page, `file-tree-explorer.html`, and its data file, `file-tree.data.json`. The page is on claude.ai at https://claude.ai/artifact/72v2Uppt6jpfXLCjKNX9xs.
- `server/` operates the same page on the owner's server. Claude Code operates behind the request box of the page.
- The server files are `server.py`, `claude_bridge.py`, `voice.py`, `server.config.json` and `README.md`. `voice.py` changes speech to text with Groq.
- `data/` is the planned location of the project records: inputs, decisions, changelog, tree notes, knowledge map, plans, working notes, the page store and the archive.
- During the planning, the records are in the planning area. The build copies them into `data/`.
- `docs/` contains the four docs of the IDE. Its README is the full documentation of the IDE.

The page shows each file and each folder of the repository:

- The File tab shows the text of a file. The owner can read and edit the text.
- The metadata files show as tabs: How it works, Details, Example, Questions and the ASD-STE100 version of a README.
- Some kinds of file have custom views. An example is the table of key names for a `.env` file.
- A tab shows only when its file exists.
- A "metadata" switch shows or hides the metadata files in the tree.
- Each item has a request box for questions and changes.
- On the owner's server, a voice button records the owner.
- Each item has a Delete button.
- The "Apply changes" button at the top puts all changes from the page into the files.

During the planning, start the page on the owner's server from the top of the repository with `python3 vision/server/server.py`. The server listens only on the machine, at `127.0.0.1:8765`. Use an SSH tunnel to open it.

Its docs: `apps/project-IDE/docs/README.md`.

### Keys and secrets

`.secrets/` at the top of the repository is the one location for all private keys. It is outside `agents/`. Thus no agent folder and no link can get to it.

- `.secrets/test/.env` contains all test keys.
- `.secrets/live/.env` will contain the live keys, with the same names. Only the owner writes this file.
- The two `.env` files stay on the machine. Do not put them in git.
- `.secrets/secrets.index.json` lists the key names and the files that use them. It does not contain values.
- The folder, `test/`, `live/`, the index and all How it works and Details files are in git. They show in the tree.

The page shows each `.env` file as local-only. The page does not read, show or edit the text of a `.env` file.

Settings and docs give the names of keys. They do not give the values. Two of the key names are `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, for Claude Code on the server, and `GROQ_API_KEY`, for voice input.

`.gitignore` keeps all `.env` files out of git. An `.env.example` file is the exception, because it contains only names. `.gitignore` keeps the How it works, Details and Questions files of a keys file in git. It also keeps these items out of git:

- dependencies and build output: `node_modules/`, `dist/`, `build/`, `.venv/` and `venv/`
- Python caches
- OS files and editor files
- the local state of Cursor

Each entry in `.gitignore` has a comment that tells why.

Its docs: `.secrets/.secrets.index.md` and `.gitignore.index.md`.

### Metadata files

Each file and each folder outside the planning area has metadata files next to it. The name of a metadata file is the name of the item without its extension.

| Metadata file | Tab on the page | Content |
|---|---|---|
| `x.index.md` | How it works | What the item is, who keeps it, when and how it changes, who uses it, where other files mention it, related knowledge, and a maximum of four "keep in mind" lines, in plain words |
| `x.meta.json` | Details | The facts about the item: its kind, its state, git or secret, who writes it, who reads it, when it changes, related files, sources, what must change with it, and what applies from the levels above |
| `x.example.md` | Example | The outline of the item: its sections and the content of each section |
| `x.questions.md` | Questions | The open questions for the owner about the item |
| `x.{type}.{name}.view.html` | A custom view | A view for one kind of item. It is planned |

- A folder `f/` keeps its metadata files inside it, as `f/f.index.md` and `f/f.meta.json`.
- A file without an extension keeps its full name, for example `.gitignore.index.md`.
- The metadata files of the root are `agent-os.index.md` and `agent-os.meta.json`.
- A metadata file has no metadata files.
- Now, only the main docs and the two `.env` files have Example files and Questions files. The example of a `.env` file is `.env.example`. It contains only key names.

During the planning, the source of each How it works file and each Details file is in the mirror tree of the planning area, `vision/tree/agent-os/`. The build copies each file next to its item. The knowledge base agent writes these files with the `file-index` skill. It writes the children before their folders.

Its docs: `agent-os.index.md` and the `file-index` skill, `agents/system/.claude/skills/file-index/SKILL.md`.

### The planning area

`vision/` contains all the material that we use to plan the project. It is the workshop. The other parts of the repository are the system as we design it.

- `vision/docs/` is the knowledge base.
- `vision/docs/inputs/` keeps each owner input word for word, with its answer. It also has `index.json`.
- `vision/docs/decisions.md` keeps all decisions.
- `vision/docs/changelog.md` records the changes. The newest change is first.
- `vision/docs/file-tree.md` contains the tree notes: the planned tree and one section for each file and each folder.
- `vision/docs/` also contains topic notes for agents: `overview.md`, `architecture.md`, `conventions.md`, `safety.md`, `flows.md`, `data-schemas.md`, `glossary.md`, `metrics.md`, `roadmap.md`, `feature-map.md`, `common/`, `how-to/` and `index/`. `index/` contains the knowledge map.
- `vision/docs/prediction-market-agents/` contains the notes of the prediction-market domain.
- `vision/plans/` contains one plan for each change request, and `index.json`.
- `vision/.claude/` contains the planning copies of the helper agents, the skills and the working memory (`memory/`). It also contains the notes behind each doc (`knowledge/sources/`).
- `vision/tools/` contains the build scripts: `parse.py`, `enrich.py`, `materialize.py`, `tabs.py`, `build_map.py`, `index_files.py` and `check_page.js`. It also contains `overrides.json`, which keeps the owner's page edits in the data.
- `vision/explorer/` contains the page source, its data and the texts of the real files that the page shows.
- `vision/server/` contains the server of the page. During the planning, the server operates from here.
- `vision/tree/agent-os/` is the mirror tree of all How it works files and Details files.
- `vision/archive/` keeps old texts, by date. It includes the old drafts of the docs and the files of the prediction-market domain for stage two.

The build copies the drafts, records and metadata files from `vision/` to their locations in the tree. We write the docs of each level in their own folders.

It is an open subject when the real files become the only source. After that change, `vision/` becomes an archive.

Its docs: `vision/docs/README.md` and `vision/tools/README.md`.

## How a round of work goes

Each round has the same steps. The source of the round can be a chat, the page or the work of the AI.

1. Pull the latest `main` into the working branch.
2. Keep the owner's input word for word in `vision/docs/inputs/`. Use the `knowledge-intake` skill. Add a summary, the categories and the answer. Keep a question and its answer as one input.
3. Write a plan in `vision/plans/` with the `change-plan` skill. Show the plan to the owner. Start the work only after the owner approves it. A small fix does not need a plan.
4. Update the docs of each level that the change touches. Use this order in each level: `vision.md`, `README.md`, `README.asd.md`, `rebuild-prompt.md`.
5. Use this order of levels: project, system, apps, project IDE, trading. When a lower level changes, update the levels above it.
6. Write the decisions in `vision/docs/decisions.md`. Write a line in `vision/docs/changelog.md`.
7. Write each stale How it works file and Details file again with `file-index`. Do the children first. Continue until no file is stale.
8. Build the page again with `ide-build`. If the owner pushed "Apply changes", do `ide-sync` first.
9. The build does these steps: parse, enrich, materialize, check the How it works files, write `docs/file-tree.md`, test the page and publish it at the same link.
10. Compare the page tree with the disk. The page tree must list the same files as git (`git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard`), and the two local-only `.env` files.
11. Commit the change. The message must tell what changed and which input caused the change.
12. Open or update a pull request into `main`.
13. Merge only when the owner tells you to merge.

## The stages

Stage one is the current stage. In stage one, we do this work:

1. Complete the project IDE and its full documentation.
2. Examine each file and each folder. Write the custom views. Make all metadata correct.
3. Complete the docs of the project, the system, trading and the apps.

In stage one, do not change the contents of the prediction-market domain.

Stage two is the prediction-market domain: its docs, its strategies and their trading agents. The old files of the domain wait in the archive of the planning area.

After stage two, we build the machinery of the system. We start the first strategy in test mode. We add more trading domains and agents of other kinds.

## Where each part's docs are

| Part | Its docs | Content |
|---|---|---|
| The full project | `docs/vision.md`, `docs/README.md` | Why, the method of work and each part of the repository |
| The front page | `README.index.md` | The purpose of the front page |
| The handoff | `HANDOFF.index.md` | The purpose of the handoff |
| All paths | `docs/file-tree.md` | The plain list of the repository |
| The entry point for Claude Code | `agents/system/CLAUDE.md` | What to read first, the rules and the round |
| Agents | `agents/agents.index.md` | The domains and the standard folder |
| The system | `agents/system/docs/README.md` | The exact description of each shared part of the system |
| Trading | `agents/trading/docs/README.md` | The trading domains and their research |
| The prediction-market domain | `agents/trading/prediction-market/docs/` | Stage two. Only the folder exists |
| Apps | `apps/docs/README.md` | Each app and how we add apps |
| The project IDE | `apps/project-IDE/docs/README.md` | The full documentation of the IDE |
| The IDE server | `apps/project-IDE/server/README.md` | How to operate the page on the owner's server |
| Keys | `.secrets/.secrets.index.md` | How we keep keys |
| Git ignore rules | `.gitignore.index.md` | Each ignore rule |
| Metadata files | `agent-os.index.md`, `agents/system/.claude/skills/file-index/SKILL.md` | How to write each How it works file |
| The planning area | `vision/docs/README.md`, `vision/tools/README.md` | The knowledge base and the build |

## Still open in the design

- Doc names: Do we keep the name `rebuild-prompt.md`, or do we change it to `reverse-prompt.md`?
- Repository name: Do we change the name of the repository and its top folder to `agent-os`?
- Front page: What does `README.md` at the top tell? It is empty now.
- Planning area: When do the real files become the only source? When does `vision/` become an archive? Until then, the build copies the drafts to their locations.
- Records: Do the records move from `vision/docs/` to `apps/project-IDE/data/`, as planned?
- Plain file tree: Do we add some information to each line of `docs/file-tree.md` later?
- Metadata tabs: Which other files get Example, Questions, Tests and changelog files? Which custom views does each kind of item get?
- Folder names in the prediction-market domain: Do the strategy folders and the trading agent folders keep their current names?

# README.asd.md

## What it is

The project README again, in ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English: the same content and section order as `README.md`, in short, simple, active sentences, so the owner can compare the two versions. `README.md` is its source.

## Who looks after it

The knowledge base agent, with the `readme-asd-doc` skill. The owner can also change it on the File Tree page; a change that is not in `README.md` goes into `README.md` first.

## When and how it changes

Every time `README.md` changes, right after it and before the rebuild prompt. The agent rewrites the changed sections under the ASD-STE100 rules: one topic per sentence, at most 25 words for a description and 20 for an instruction, present tense, one word for one meaning, numbered steps for procedures.

## Who uses it, and when

The owner, to compare it with the README and to read the project in the simplest words. Any reader or AI that wants short, unambiguous sentences.

## Where it is mentioned

`README.md` names it, the File Tree page shows it as the ASD-STE100 tab of the README, and the `readme-asd-doc` skill.

## Related knowledge

`README.md` is the only source of its content; it adds nothing of its own. The archived inputs vision in `vision/archive/` is the model for its style.

## Keep in mind

- When it and `README.md` disagree, `README.md` is right: fix this file.
- When you write it, use the names in `README.md` exactly.

# Open questions: docs/README.asd.md

- **Should the page show `README.asd.md` as an "ASD-STE100" tab on `README.md`, or as its own file only?** The plan proposes a tab; it decides how the owner compares the two versions.

# Rebuild the Agent OS repository: the top level

## Your task
Who the agent is, what this prompt builds (the top level only) and what the lower prompts build, what it never does, and how to work.

## The project in brief
The Agent OS and the way it is built, in about 300 words, in the vision's words.

## Ground rules
Keys, formats, names, metadata files, docs for people, git.

## The repository tree
The top level as one code block, every entry with a one-line comment; lower-prompt and copied lines marked.

## Conventions
The docs every level has and where; the ASD-STE100 rules; the formats of the How it works, Details, Example and Questions files, each with an example.

## The parts
One section per top part, each with the files to create, what they hold, and its check.

### Root files
### .gitignore
### .secrets/
### docs/
### agents/ and apps/
### vision/

## Build order
Numbered steps, ending with the lower prompts in order: system, apps (then the project IDE), trading.

The list that proves the top level is the same.

Open points and later stages, one line each, with what to leave in their place.

nodes.content:
# Rebuild the Agent OS repository: the top level

## Your task

You are an AI coding agent, such as Claude Code, in an empty git repository. Build the top level of the Agent OS repository so that it ends up the same as the repository it was written from: the same top folders and files, the same names and formats, the same keys folder without any key value, the same project docs and the same metadata files. Then build every level below it by following that level's own rebuild prompt, in the order under "Build order". "The same repository" means every check under "Acceptance checks" passes.

This prompt builds only the top level: the root files, `.gitignore`, `.secrets/`, `docs/`, and the top folders `agents/` and `apps/` with their own metadata files. It never builds the inside of a level; each level's prompt does that. The planning folder `vision/` is not built from a spec: it is the project's record, copied in as the owner hands it to you.

Never do any of these:

- Write a key value anywhere: in a file, a commit, a log, a prompt or a message. Key names only.
- Create a `.env` file with content, read one, or add one to git.
- Act in the outside world: publish the File Tree page, push, open or merge a pull request, without the owner's word. Commit only when the owner asks.
- Create any file inside `agents/trading/prediction-market/`: it is stage two, folders only.
- Install anything globally, or register a background service or a scheduled job.

How to work:

- Follow "Build order" step by step. Run each step's check and fix any failure before the next step.
- Build what this file states, including what is marked "default, the owner may change it".
- Where this file says a point is open, leave what it says in its place and list the point in your report. Never invent an answer.
- Where you must choose a detail this file does not settle, choose the simplest thing that passes the checks, write it down as "default, the owner may change it" in that item's How it works file, and report it.
- If the owner hands you material from the current repository (the planning folder, the research studies, the page, the server, the drafts), copy it in unchanged at the path this file or a lower prompt names, then check it.
- Call the owner "the owner", and "they" when a pronoun is needed.
- When you finish, report in short plain lines: what you built, every default you chose, every open point you left, and the result of every acceptance check.

## The project in brief

The Agent OS is the owner's personal system for running AI agents of any kind: agents that trade, that work on social media or that help with management. It runs many small agents side by side, each with one clear job, tries every idea safely in test mode first and keeps what works. Trading on prediction markets is its first area of work. Nothing of the system runs yet.

The owner builds it by vibecoding: they say what they want in plain words, and AI writes the plans, the docs and later the code. Every input is kept word for word, every change gets a plan the owner sees first, and the docs at every level are brought in line in a fixed order. The owner follows everything through the project IDE: the File Tree page, a clickable map of every file and folder with a plain How it works for each, on claude.ai and on the owner's server with Claude Code behind its request box.

The repository is described in levels: the project (the whole repository, in `docs/`), the system (`agents/system/docs/`), trading (`agents/trading/docs/`), the apps (`apps/docs/`) and each app, the project IDE first (`apps/project-IDE/docs/`). Each level has a vision, a README, the README again in ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English, and a rebuild prompt. Every file and folder has metadata files beside it. Keys stay on the machine: only their names are in git.

The project is in stage one: finish the project IDE, make all metadata correct, and write the docs at the project, system, trading and apps levels. The prediction-market domain is stage two and exists only as folders.

## Ground rules

**Keys.** Every private key lives only in `.secrets/` at the repository root. `.secrets/test/.env` and `.secrets/live/.env` hold the values and never go into git; everything else in `.secrets/` does. Settings and docs name keys, never values. The File Tree page lists a `.env` file as local-only and never reads, shows or edits it.

**Formats.** Markdown for docs and notes, JSON for settings, indexes and Details files. UTF-8, LF line endings, no BOM. JSON pretty-printed with 2 spaces. Every JSON file you own starts with `"schema_version": 1`, except an empty `{}` placeholder and the tool files that have their own format.

**Names.** File and folder names are exact as written here, character for character. Names in `[brackets]` are placeholders and are created as written. In a name, `|` becomes `-`.

**Metadata files.** Every file and folder outside `vision/` has metadata files beside it, named after the item without its extension:

- `x.index.md`: How it works, plain prose for people.
- `x.meta.json`: Details, the facts about the item.
- `x.example.md`: the item's outline; only for the main docs and the `.env` files for now.
- `x.questions.md`: open questions for the owner; only for the main docs and the `.env` files for now.

A file `vision.md` has `vision.index.md`; a file without an extension keeps its whole name (`.gitignore.index.md`); a folder `f/` keeps its own inside it (`f/f.index.md`, `f/f.meta.json`); the repository root, standing for `agent-os/`, has `agent-os.index.md` and `agent-os.meta.json`. When two names in a folder would be the same, or a file is named like its folder, the file keeps its extension (`server.py.index.md`). A metadata file has no metadata files of its own. The `.env` files' Example is `.env.example`, holding key names only.

**Docs for people.** The vision and the README of every level are plain, book-like prose: no reference numbers, no decision or input codes, no history. Paths are fine in a README.

**Git.** Everything that defines the project is committed. Keys files, dependencies, caches and editor state are not. A folder with nothing in it keeps a `.gitkeep`.

## The repository tree

The top level, as you build it. Lines marked "lower prompt" are built by that level's own prompt; lines marked "copied" are copied from what the owner hands you.

```text

├── README.meta.json

├── HANDOFF.index.md

├── .gitignore                     # exactly as under "The parts"
├── .gitignore.index.md

│   ├── .secrets.index.md
```

## Conventions

**Docs per level.** Every level's `docs/` folder holds `vision.md`, `README.md`, `README.asd.md` and `rebuild-prompt.md`, written in that order. The project level adds `file-tree.md`. Each doc has its How it works and Details files; the four written docs also have their Example and Questions files. Levels, with their docs folders:

| Level | Docs folder |
|---|---|
| Project | `docs/` |
| System | `agents/system/docs/` |
| Trading | `agents/trading/docs/` |
| Prediction-market domain (stage two) | `agents/trading/prediction-market/docs/` (folder only) |
| Apps | `apps/docs/` |
| Project IDE | `apps/project-IDE/docs/` |

**`README.asd.md`.** The README of its level again, with the same content and section order, in ASD-STE100: one topic per sentence; descriptive sentences at most 25 words, procedural sentences at most 20; active voice; present tense; approved simple words; one word for one meaning, the names exactly as in `README.md`; numbered steps for procedures; paragraphs of at most six sentences. Its first line says it is the ASD-STE100 version of `README.md` and that `README.md` is the source.

**How it works file.** Front matter, then one heading with the item's name, then six fixed headings, then "Keep in mind":

```markdown
---
about: agent-os/docs/vision.md
node: n-57.1
written: 2026-10-12T00:00:00Z
by: knowledge-base-agent
---
# vision.md

## What it is
## Who looks after it
## When and how it changes
## Who uses it, and when
## Where it is mentioned
## Related knowledge

## Keep in mind

- When you ..., ...
```

`about` is the path from `agent-os/`; `node` is the item's id on the File Tree page (`n-` and its number in the tree notes). A file not yet moved to this format has one `## Summary` instead of the six headings. The build adds a `basis` line and may add `confirmed`; never write them by hand.

**Details file.** JSON with exactly these fields, filled where known and empty otherwise:

```json
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "about": "What it is for, in one line.",
  "kind": "file",
  "state": "written",
  "status": "decided",
  "git": "tracked",
  "secret": false,
  "generated_by": null,
  "writers": ["the knowledge base agent (vision-doc skill)"],
  "readers": ["the owner", "every AI session"],
  "changes_when": "an input changes the project as a whole",
  "related": [{"path": "docs/README.md", "how": "follows it"}],
  "sources": {"decisions": [], "inputs": [], "notes": []},
  "update_with": [{"path": "docs/README.md", "how": "same words for the same things"}],
  "inherits": [],
  "features": [],
  "views": [],
  "how_it_works": {"written": "2026-10-12T00:00:00Z", "by": "knowledge-base-agent"},
  "tree_number": "57.1"
}
```

`kind` is `file`, `folder`, `file link` or `folder link`; `state` is `written`, `not written yet`, `built` or `name pattern`; `status` is `decided`, `proposed` or `example`; `git` is `tracked` or `ignored`. An item with nothing known yet gets the same fields with empty values.

**Example file.** The doc's outline as a Markdown skeleton: its title, each heading in order, and one line under each saying what goes there.

**Questions file.** One short question per line item for the owner, each with a sentence on why it matters, or the line "None open."

## The parts

### Root files

- `README.md`: create it empty. What the front page says is open; do not write it.
- `HANDOFF.md`: copy it as the owner hands it to you. If you have none, do not create it.
- `agent-os.index.md`: How it works of the whole repository in at most 200 words: what the Agent OS is, the top folders and what each holds, the stage, and up to four system-wide "Keep in mind" lines (key names only, never a value; the page tree equals the disk; decided only on the owner's word; plan every change).
- Every root file gets its How it works and Details files.

Check: `ls` at the root shows exactly the root entries of the tree above (plus `.git/`).

### .gitignore

Write it exactly:

```text
# Keys files never go in git: every .env (the keys folder .secrets/ itself and its notes do)
.env
.env.*
!.env.example
# How it works and Details files of a keys file hold no keys, so they stay in git
!.env.index.md
!.env.meta.json
!.env.questions.md

# Dependencies and build output
node_modules/
dist/
build/
.venv/
venv/

# Python
__pycache__/
*.py[cod]
*.egg-info/
.pytest_cache/
.mypy_cache/

# OS and editor
.DS_Store
*.swp
.idea/
.vscode/

# Cursor local state
.cursor/
```

Every new ignore line gets a comment saying why.

Check: `git check-ignore .secrets/test/.env .secrets/live/.env` prints both paths; `git check-ignore .secrets/test/.env.index.md .secrets/test/.env.example .secrets/test/.env.questions.md` prints nothing.

### .secrets/

Create `.secrets/`, `.secrets/test/` and `.secrets/live/`. Set the folder to `chmod 700` and each `.env` file to `chmod 600` (default, the owner may change it).

- `.secrets/test/.env` and `.secrets/live/.env`: create each empty, only if it does not exist. Never read, overwrite or commit one. Only the owner puts values in them; only the owner ever touches `live/.env`.
- `.secrets/test/.env.example` and `.secrets/live/.env.example`: the key names, one `NAME=` per line under comment sections, with no values; the only line with a value is the mode, `AGENT_OS_ENV=test` in the test file and `AGENT_OS_ENV=live` in the live file, which is not a secret. Today the names include `AGENT_OS_ENV`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (Claude Code on the owner's server) and `GROQ_API_KEY` (voice input on the page), `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` and `NOTIFY_TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`; take the full list from the owner's material or from the system's prompt.
- `.secrets/secrets.index.json`: `{}` until the first key is listed; then `"schema_version": 1` and, per key name, what kind it is, its mode and what uses it. Never a value.
- How it works, Details and Questions files as in the tree.

Check: `git ls-files .secrets` lists no file named `.env`; `grep '=.' .secrets/*/.env.example` prints only the two `AGENT_OS_ENV` lines.

### docs/

Write the project docs in this order, each with its own skill when the skills exist (`vision-doc`, `readme-doc`, `readme-asd-doc`, `rebuild-prompt-doc`):

1. `docs/vision.md`: what the Agent OS project is and why; the way of working (vibecoding, the project IDE as the owner's window); the concept (the system, the levels of docs, metadata next to everything, the way of working, the IDE, the planning area); a round of work as a story; the rules the project follows; examples; what the owner sees and does; the stages; principles; ideas still weighed; open questions; and last, the path `docs/README.md`. Plain prose, no paths except that one.
2. `docs/README.md`: every part of the repository exactly, with the path to each part's own docs: the front page and handoff, the project docs, agents, the system with `agents/system/CLAUDE.md`, trading, apps, the project IDE, keys, metadata files, the planning area; then how a round of work goes, the stages, a table of every part's docs, and what is still open.
3. `docs/README.asd.md`: `README.md` again in ASD-STE100, as under "Conventions".
4. `docs/rebuild-prompt.md`: this file.
5. Each doc's Example and Questions files.
6. `docs/file-tree.md`: never written by hand. The IDE build writes it every round: every path in the repository, one per line, in tree order, with nothing else on the line. Until the build exists, create it empty.

If the owner handed you the current docs, copy them in unchanged instead of writing them, then check them against this list.

Check: the five docs and their metadata files exist; `docs/README.asd.md` has the same `##` headings, in the same order, as `docs/README.md`.

### agents/ and apps/

Create `agents/` and `apps/`, each with its own How it works and Details files. `agents/agents.index.md` says that every child is a domain, the system is one, trading is a folder of domains, and every agent has the same standard folder. `apps/apps.index.md` says what apps are (our own, outside ones we fork, research clones in `temp/`) and names the project IDE. Everything inside them is built by the lower prompts.

Check: both folders and their two metadata files exist.

### vision/

The planning area is the project's record while it is planned: the knowledge base with every owner input word for word, the decisions and the changelog (`vision/docs/`), the plans (`vision/plans/`), the planning copies of the helper agents and skills (`vision/.claude/`), the build scripts (`vision/tools/`), the page source (`vision/explorer/`), the page's server (`vision/server/`), the mirror of every How it works and Details file (`vision/tree/agent-os/`) and the archive (`vision/archive/`). Never write it from this prompt and never invent its content: copy it in unchanged as the owner hands it to you. If you have none, create only `vision/` with an empty `docs/inputs/` folder and report it. Items inside `vision/` get no metadata files.

Check: when copied, `git diff --stat` against the owner's material shows no change under `vision/`.

## Build order

1. Write the root files and `.gitignore`. Check: the root files and `.gitignore` checks.
2. Create `.secrets/` (never any key value). Check: the `.secrets/` checks.
3. Copy `vision/` if the owner handed it to you. Check: the `vision/` check.
4. Create `agents/` and `apps/` with their metadata files. Check: their check.
5. Write or copy `docs/` (step 6 of its list waits for the build). Check: the `docs/` check.
6. Follow the lower rebuild prompts, in this order, running each one's own checks:
   1. `agents/system/docs/rebuild-prompt.md`: the system agent, the shared parts, `agents/system/CLAUDE.md`, the helper agents and skills, the build scripts.
   2. `apps/docs/rebuild-prompt.md`: the apps folder, `apps/temp/`, `apps/trading-ui/`, and in its turn `apps/project-IDE/docs/rebuild-prompt.md`, the File Tree page, its server and its data.
   3. `agents/trading/docs/rebuild-prompt.md`: the folder of trading domains, its research studies, and the prediction-market domain as folders only (stage two).
   If a prompt in this list is still empty, create that level's folder with its four docs as empty files and their metadata files, report it, and go on.
7. Write every missing or stale How it works file with the `file-index` skill, children before their folders, until `build_map.py --stale` prints nothing.
8. Run the IDE build (`ide-build`), which also writes `docs/file-tree.md`. Check: the page check prints "page ok".
9. Run every acceptance check and report to the owner.

## Acceptance checks

1. The root holds exactly the entries of the tree above, and every file and folder outside `vision/` has its `x.index.md` and `x.meta.json`.
2. No key value is in git: `git ls-files | grep -E '(^|/)\.env$'` prints nothing, and for every key name listed in `secrets.index.json` or an `.env.example`, `git grep -E "<NAME>=.+"` finds nothing.
3. Every JSON file you wrote parses (`python3 -m json.tool <file>`).
4. `docs/` holds the five docs with their metadata files, and `README.asd.md` follows `README.md` section by section.
5. Every lower prompt in the build order ran and its checks passed, or it was empty and is reported.
6. `agents/trading/prediction-market/` holds folders, `.gitkeep` files and nothing else.
7. `build_map.py --stale` and `build_map.py --orphans` print nothing.
8. The page tree equals the disk: the paths the page lists are exactly `git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard`, plus the two local-only `.env` files.
9. `docs/file-tree.md` lists the same paths.
10. Nothing was pushed, published or merged without the owner's word.

## Do not build

Leave each as stated, and list it in your report.

- The front page text: `README.md` stays empty.
- A new name for the rebuild prompt (`reverse-prompt.md`): keep `rebuild-prompt.md`.
- A new name for the repository or its top folder: keep them.
- Retiring the planning copies so the real files are the only source: keep the build copying from `vision/`.
- Moving the records from `vision/docs/` into `apps/project-IDE/data/`: only the build's copies go there.
- Extra information on each line of `docs/file-tree.md`: none.
- Example, Questions, Tests and changelog files for items other than the main docs and the `.env` files: none.
- Custom views (`x.{type}.{name}.view.html`): none from this prompt.
- Anything inside `agents/trading/prediction-market/` beyond its folders: nothing; it is stage two.
- The copy-trading domain and any other domain not in a lower prompt: nothing.
- Live keys, live actions and anything that acts in the outside world: nothing.

# Open questions: docs/rebuild-prompt.md

- **Should a rebuilt repository include `vision/` at all, or only the system as designed?** Today the prompt copies the planning area as the owner hands it over; once the real files are the only source, it could be left out.

# file-tree.md

## What it is

A plain list of every path in the repository, one per line, with nothing else on the line: no comments, numbers or other metadata. It gives people and AI a fast, exact map of what exists.

## Who looks after it

The project IDE agent, with the `ide-build` skill: the build writes it. Nobody writes it by hand.

## When and how it changes

Every round, when the page is built: the build lists the paths in the repository and writes the file again, so it always matches the disk and the page.

## Who uses it, and when

Claude Code started in the system folder reads it after the project and system docs, to know what exists. The owner and any agent use it to find a file fast.

## Where it is mentioned

`agents/system/CLAUDE.md` (the reading list), the project README and rebuild prompt, and the `ide-build` skill.

## Related knowledge

It lists the same paths as the File Tree page and as git (`git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard`). The tree notes in `vision/docs/file-tree.md` are a different file: the planned tree with one section per item. Adding a little information to each line later is an idea still weighed.

## Keep in mind

- When it looks wrong, fix the build and rebuild; never edit it by hand.

nodes.name: .secrets/
nodes.summary: SECRETS STORE (D-023): in git without the .env files (D-063), chmod 700, outside agents/
nodes.purpose: the single store for private keys, wallet keys, API keys and tokens for outside accounts (such as the prediction-market domain's trading accounts, [19.2.4] `accounts`) and platforms [11.11] `platforms`.

details.label: Location (proposed)
details.text: repo root, **outside `agents/`**, so no agent or level session (which run inside `agents/…`) has it in its folder, and no `subagents.link/` or file link reaches it. Git-ignored via [48]. Folder `chmod 700`, files `chmod 600`, owned by the user that runs the scripts. Stronger option: keep it outside the repo entirely (e.g. `~/.agent-os/secrets/`) with the same layout.

details.label: Contents (D-027 updates D-023)
details.text: [47.1] `test/.env` holds **all** test keys in one file (`KEY=value`, keys prefixed per account/platform, e.g. `POLYMARKET_ACCT1_API_KEY` in the prediction-market domain); [47.2] `live/.env` will mirror it with the same key names and live values (later phase; the owner decides per key which values stay the same and which change, e.g. real-money accounts). Splitting into one file per account can come later if the file gets unwieldy. [47.3] `secrets.index.json` with metadata only: `{ "[ref]": { "kind": "wallet|api-key|token", "env": "test|live", "used_by": ["[account-id]"], "created", "rotate_by" } }`, never values.

details.label: Access (D-027)
details.text: agents and the dev workflow may read and update `test/.env` (safe test credentials; content grows with the project, no fixed schema yet). Nobody but the owner writes `live/.env`; agents never get write access to it. Each level's `.claude/settings.json` denies `.secrets/live/**` (not all of `.secrets/**` any more).

details.label: Loading (proposed, D-027)
details.text: nothing opens the file inline. An agent or worker declares the keys it needs in its own config (e.g. `"secret_keys": ["POLYMARKET_ACCT1_*"]`). The shared loader `load-secret` [14.1] (shell + Python twin) reads `.secrets/[test|live]/.env` and exports only those keys into the child process of that run: `load-secret POLYMARKET_ACCT1_* -- python3 scripts/get-polymarket-data.worker.py`. The mode comes from `AGENT_OS_ENV` (default `test`); `live` is refused unless the run is owner-approved. A missing key fails fast with the key name. The loader logs only key names, mode and result, never values.

details.label: Editing from a UI (owner request)
details.text: create/edit keys from the local trading UI [45] (it runs next to the files; values never leave the machine). The planning explorer page cannot and should not hold secret values.

details.label: Access rule (proposed)
details.text:
- Agents never get a link or copy of anything in here; `check-links` [14.1] fails on any link or file whose target is inside `.secrets/`.
- Configs hold only key names (`secret_keys`, D-027) or refs ([19.2.4] `accounts`, [11.11] `platforms`), never values.
- Scripts that act (executor/decision [14.3], [33]; workers that call private APIs) call `load-secret` [14.1] at execution time. It returns the value only if that agent's config references the ref, and `live/` refs only if the owner approved the agent for live ([11.1] `modes`; in the prediction-market domain also a funded, owner-approved account, [19.2.4] `accounts`).
- **Live values never in LLM context:** they are passed to the script process only (env injection), never into prompts or Claude Code sessions. Each level's `.claude/settings.json` ([10.1.6], [19.1.6], [21.1.6], [24.6]) denies `.secrets/live/**`. Test values may be seen by an agent that updates `test/.env` (D-027); they are still never copied into configs, docs, data or logs.
- **Never logged:** loggers redact anything resolved by `load-secret`; [2.14] schemas forbid secret fields in data/logs.

details.label: Test vs live
details.text: separate folders and separate refs. A test agent can never resolve a `live/` ref.

details.label: Rotation (proposed)
details.text: `rotate_by` in [47.3]. The notifier warns before expiry. Rotation writes a new value under the same ref (configs stay unchanged), then revokes the old key at the provider. Runbook in [2.11.6].

details.label: Upgrade path (later)
details.text: replace the file backend of `load-secret` with the OS keychain, a password manager CLI (e.g. 1Password) or a vault (e.g. HashiCorp Vault). The `secret_keys` lists and the configs stay the same.

nodes.writers_readers: the owner writes live keys; agents may read and update the test `.env` (D-027). Scripts get only the keys their config declares, through `load-secret` [14.1].

features.logic: Keys: stored in a git-ignored store, test/live separated, loaded by scripts at execution time, never linked, logged or put in LLM context (D-023, proposed)

Scripts get keys only through `load-secret`, at run time, and only the names their config lists.

# .secrets/test/.env: the key names this file holds, with no values.
# The real .env stays on the machine and never goes in git. Type real values only there.

# Which secrets file load-secret reads: test or live. test | live, required. Used by load-secret.
AGENT_OS_ENV=test

# Claude API for agents and sub-agents run headless. sk-ant-..., required. Used by run-agent, run-tests.
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=

# Polymarket CLOB API key for test account 1. uuid, required. Used by acct-pm-test-1, polymarket-exec.
POLYMARKET_ACCT1_API_KEY=

# Secret paired with the API key. base64, required. Used by acct-pm-test-1.
POLYMARKET_ACCT1_API_SECRET=

# Passphrase paired with the API key. text, required. Used by acct-pm-test-1.
POLYMARKET_ACCT1_API_PASSPHRASE=

# Signs orders for the account's wallet. 0x + 64 hex, required. Used by acct-pm-test-1.
POLYMARKET_ACCT1_WALLET_PRIVATE_KEY=

# Groq speech to text for voice input in the project IDE (D-060); test file only. gsk_..., optional. Used by apps/project-IDE/server/voice.py.
GROQ_API_KEY=

# Other models via OpenRouter (not connected yet). sk-or-..., optional. Used by models.config.json.
OPENROUTER_API_KEY=

# Alerts to Telegram (later). 123:ABC..., optional. Used by notifier.
NOTIFY_TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN=

# agents/

## Summary

All agents of the Agent OS, one folder per domain. The system is a domain too: `system/` holds the system agent and everything every agent shares, whatever its domain. `trading/` is a folder of trading domains with trading's own docs; its first domain, `trading/prediction-market/`, holds everything about trading today, and the next, `trading/copytrading/`, will be copied from it. Inside the prediction-market domain sit its strategy agents, and inside each strategy its trading agents, one per version being tested.

Every level uses one identical agent folder: `.claude/` with the level's prompt, then `configs/`, `scripts/`, `logs/`, `data/`, `docs/`, `tests/`, `research/` and the level files. Each content folder holds the level's own files, file links to what it reads elsewhere, and `subagents.link/` to its children. Agents are created by `create-agent`, and self-improvement creates new test versions. Secrets, the apps and cloned code live outside this folder.

## Keep in mind

- When you add an agent, give it a unique name and the standard folder through `create-agent`; never copy a folder by hand.
- When an agent needs another agent's file, add a link to its links file; it never writes into another agent's folder.

nodes.purpose: the system domain and the **system-level agent** (D-022): it manages all domains and the development of the system. It has the standard agent folder [2.7.1]; the only difference is that it (a) holds the **shared** files every agent uses and (b), like every level, links to its children: each content folder has `subagents.link/[domain-name]/` → that domain's folder of the same kind ([2.7.4], D-030). Strategies and agents are reached one level further down each time. This replaces the flat views of every agent (D-015).

details.label: Child links, not copies
details.text: `data/subagents.link/[domain-name]/` etc. are **folder links** to each child's real folder. Copies would duplicate data and drift out of date.

details.label: Level files (D-022)
details.text: [10.1.5] `.claude/CLAUDE.md` holds the project's rules every Claude reads first (D-045) and the system manager prompt (oversees domains, system health, system development, answers owner questions about the whole system) · [10.4] `package.json`, [10.5] `requirements.txt` for the shared scripts · [10.6] `init.sh` installs the git hooks and runs relink for the whole project (D-031) · [10.7] `start.sh` starts the scheduler [14.1] (every agent's jobs, D-029) and the system session.

details.label: Contents
details.text: [10.1] `.claude/` · [2] `docs/` · [11] `configs/` · [10.1.5] `.claude/CLAUDE.md`, [10.4]–[10.7] level files · [14] `scripts/` · [15] `logs/` · [16] `data/` · [10.8] `tests/`, [10.9] `research/` (D-025, [2.7.3]). System-support roles are sub-agents in [10.1.1] (D-026), such as the knowledge agent [10.1.1.2].

details.label: Belongs here
details.text: anything shared by two or more agents. Anything for one agent stays in that agent's folder (real files). **Promotion rule (proposed):** when a second agent needs an agent-local thing (e.g. [31]), it moves into the matching shared folder here, and agents that need it get a file link to it (D-020).

details.label: Link mechanics (proposed)
details.text:
- All links use relative paths and always have `.link` in the name ([2.7]).
- **Agent links are individual file links (D-020, supersedes D-014's folder links for agents):** inside an agent's `configs/`, `scripts/`, `logs/`, `data/`, `docs/`, each link points to **one file** its logic needs, from any folder: system (e.g. [11.1], [16.3]), domain (e.g. [14.3], [19.5.3]) or strategy level, or another agent's outputs. Examples: [27.1], [30.1], [34.1], [35.1], [46.1]. There are no `system.link/` folders in agents any more.
- **Which links (D-031):** each agent lists them in its own links file `configs/[name].links.json` ([11.13] system, [19.2.3] domain, [21.2.3] strategy, [27.3] variant). `create-agent` [14.1] writes the first version; afterwards the agent itself, its SI sub-agent or the owner edit it. A link may come from anywhere under `agents/`: the system, the agent's own domain or strategy, another domain, or another agent (by unique name). The shared `relink` script [14.1] builds every link from these files.
- **Stable targets (proposed):** producers keep a stable file per output (e.g. `latest.json`, `latest.md`, `latest.log`), so file links do not break when dated files rotate.
- **No `.claude` links (D-030, for now):** the D-019 down-links [10.1.3]/[10.1.4] and [21.1.3]/[21.1.4] are removed; the domain level never had any (D-021).
- **Child links (D-030):** every level's content folders hold `subagents.link/[child-name]/` → the child's folder of the same kind: system [11.2.1], [14.4.1], [15.5.1], [16.4.1], [2.20.1], [10.8.3.1], [10.9.3.1] → domains; domain [19.2.2.1], [19.3.1.1], [19.4.1.1], [19.5.1.1], [19.6.1.1], [19.12.3.1], [19.13.3.1] → strategies; strategy [21.2.2.1], [21.3.1.1], [21.4.1.1], [21.5.1.1], [21.6.1.1], [21.12.3.1], [21.13.3.1] → its agents.
- `relink` [14.1] creates the agent's file links **and** its entries in the parent's `subagents.link/` folders, and removes links nobody wants any more. `init.sh` [40] and `create-agent` call it; after `stop-or-delete` it removes the deleted agent's entries. When it runs is listed in [14.1].
- **Loops:** agents now hold only file links, so the old `system.link/` → view → agent cycle is gone. The `subagents.link/` entries are folder links, so tools must still **not follow `.link` folders recursively**. `check-links.system.js` [14.1] checks for cycles, broken links, symlinks that neither have `.link` nor sit in a `.link` folder, folder links outside `subagents.link/`, `subagents.link/` entries that are not a direct child's folder of the same kind, any `.claude` link, and any mismatch with [27.3].
- Agents treat every linked file as **read-only** and write only to their own real files.

details.label: When shared files change (proposed)
details.text: configs are read at the start of each run, so a change applies from the next run of every agent. The general stop switch in [11.1] `modes` is checked before every outside action (the prediction-market domain adds its order stop switch, [19.2.4], D-058).

details.label: Resolved (D-020, answers the D-019 follow-up)
details.text: agents have no `system.link/` folders. They hold individual file links to exactly what they need, chosen at creation and by self-improvement. The system views stay as they are. `.claude` keeps D-019 (parent → child folder links); D-020 applies only to `configs/`, `scripts/`, `logs/`, `data/`, `docs/`, so the two rules do not overlap. *Later (D-030):* the system views became per-level `subagents.link/` folders and the `.claude` links were removed.

open_questions: Should changes to shared configs require owner approval before they reach live agents?

# Agent OS

You are working in the repository of the Agent OS: the owner's personal system that runs AI agents of any kind. Trading on prediction markets is its first domain. Claude Code loads this file when it starts in `agents/system/`, which is how the owner starts it. If you started at the top of the repository, read this file first by hand. All paths below are from the top of the repository.

## Where the project is now: stage one

Nothing of the system runs yet. The repository already has its final shape: every planned file and folder exists, files with a draft carry its text, the rest are empty, and every item's metadata files sit next to it.

**Stage one, the current work:**

1. Finish the project IDE (the File Tree page and its server).
2. Go through every file and folder: write custom views for each kind of file, and make every metadata file correct.
3. Finish the docs at four levels: the project (`docs/`), the system domain (`agents/system/docs/`), trading in general (`agents/trading/docs/`) and the apps (`apps/docs/`, `apps/project-IDE/docs/`).

**Stage two, not now:** the prediction-market domain and everything under it (`agents/trading/prediction-market/`, its strategy and variant folders). Only its folders exist; its old files are in `vision/archive/2026-10-12/prediction-market/`. Do not add, write or plan anything there until the owner starts stage two.

## Read first, in this order

1. `docs/vision.md`: the project vision. What the Agent OS is, why, how it should work, where it stands.
2. `docs/README.md`: the project README. Every part of the repository and where its docs are.
3. `agents/system/docs/vision.md`: the system vision.
4. `agents/system/docs/README.md`: the system README.
5. `docs/file-tree.md`: every path in the repository, plain, without metadata. The IDE build writes it every round.
6. `apps/project-IDE/docs/README.md`: the IDE, in full: the page, its modes and tabs, how it is built and checked, the server, how the owner's edits come back.
7. The newest entries of `vision/docs/changelog.md` and `git log --oneline -20`: what changed since your last round.

Every `README.md` has an ASD-STE100 twin, `README.asd.md`, next to it. Read the README; the twin is for the owner to compare. Before you change a file or folder, read its How it works file: `x.index.md` beside a file `x.md`, or `f/f.index.md` inside a folder `f/`.

## Where things are

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| The project docs: vision, README, README.asd, rebuild prompt, the plain file tree | `docs/` |
| The system domain: its agent, shared configs, scripts, logs, data, tests, research, and this file | `agents/system/` |
| The system's helpers: the knowledge base agent, the project IDE agent, their skills | `agents/system/.claude/agents/`, `agents/system/.claude/skills/` |
| Trading in general, its docs and research; its domains (stage two) | `agents/trading/` |
| The apps and their docs; the project IDE; the trading dashboard (empty); research clones (never committed) | `apps/`, `apps/project-IDE/`, `apps/trading-ui/`, `apps/temp/` |
| The planning area: every owner input word for word, decisions, changelog, the tree notes, the knowledge base, plans, archive, memory, the build tools, the page source, the server | `vision/` |
| Keys: the folder and its notes are in git; the `.env` files with the values never are | `.secrets/` |

**Where to edit while we plan.** The docs at the four levels and this file are real files: edit them where they are. Everything else that came from a draft has its source in `vision/`, and the build copies it into place, so edit the source: skills and agents in `vision/.claude/`, tools in `vision/tools/`, the page in `vision/explorer/`, the server in `vision/server/`, records in `vision/docs/`, How it works and Details files in the mirror `vision/tree/agent-os/`.

## Rules (from the project memory, `vision/.claude/memory/`)

- Decided means the owner decided. Your own ideas are "proposed" until the owner says yes.
- Never write a key value anywhere: no keys, passwords or wallet details. Key names only. Never read a `.env` file.
- Docs for people are plain and book-like, with no reference numbers, ids or decision codes. The notes for agents keep the ids.
- Never change the owner's words in a stored input, and never drop their words from a How it works file they edited on the page.
- Plan every change that alters the system, its structure, code or docs (skill `change-plan`), show the plan to the owner, then build it. Small fixes need no plan.
- The page tree always equals the files on disk. Every planned item is a real file or folder.
- Every file and folder outside `vision/` has an `x.index.md` and an `x.meta.json`. The extra tab files (`x.example.md`, `x.questions.md`, `README.asd.md`) exist only where they are written; the page shows a tab only when its file exists.
- One job per code file. Group related ones in a folder, each with its own How it works.
- Generated files are rebuilt, never merged by hand: the page data, the knowledge map, `docs/file-tree.md`.
- Ask the owner before anything hard to undo: deleting, rewriting history, merging into `main`, anything that acts in the outside world. A Delete the owner pressed on the page is that ask for that one item.
- What you learn goes into the docs before the round ends. Every question the owner asks gets its answer written where they should have found it.
- Call the owner "the owner", and "they" when a pronoun is needed.

## After every input or update

1. **Pull.** On the owner's server, `git pull` on `main`. In the cloud project, bring `origin/main` into your branch first.
2. **File the input** word for word in `vision/docs/inputs/` with its row in `index.json` (skill `knowledge-intake`). Your answers to the owner and every change to the plan are filed too.
3. **Plan** the change if it alters the system (skill `change-plan`).
4. **Record** decisions in `vision/docs/decisions.md` and the change in `vision/docs/changelog.md`.
5. **Update the docs it touches**, level by level, in this order inside each level: vision, README, README.asd, rebuild prompt. Then this file, if the stage, the reading list or a rule changed.
6. **Update the metadata** of every file you changed: its How it works and Details, and its Example and Questions where they exist (skill `file-index`).
7. **Rebuild and check the page** (skill `ide-build`): the build reports every How it works fresh and no orphans, the page check passes, and the page tree equals the files in git.
8. **Commit and push**, with a message that says what changed and which input caused it. Cloud: open or update the pull request into `main`; merge only on the owner's word.

## When and how to update each doc

| A change to… | Makes stale… | Written with |
|---|---|---|
| goals, the concept, how the system should behave, business rules, the stage | the vision at that level and every level above it that mentions it | `vision-doc` |
| a part: a folder, an agent, an app, a config, a job, how parts connect | the README at that level, and the README of the level above if the part is listed there | `readme-doc` |
| any README | its `README.asd.md`, right after | `readme-asd-doc` |
| names, formats, the tree, the build order or checks | the rebuild prompt at that level | `rebuild-prompt-doc` |
| a file's purpose, content or links | its How it works, Details, Example and Questions | `file-index` |
| the stage, the reading list, the rules, the round | this file | `claude-md-doc` |
| any file or folder added, moved or removed | `docs/file-tree.md` and the page | `ide-build` |

Levels from the top: the project (`docs/`), then the system (`agents/system/docs/`), trading (`agents/trading/docs/`) and the apps (`apps/docs/`), then each app (`apps/project-IDE/docs/`). Write the lowest level that changed first, then each level above it.

## The File Tree page

The page is published at https://claude.ai/artifact/72v2Uppt6jpfXLCjKNX9xs, and the owner's server serves the same page with `python3 vision/server/server.py`. Messages, edits and deletions the owner leaves on it wait in the page's store, marked "changed". When the owner presses Apply changes, or says "sync the file tree", run `ide-sync` (everything saved word for word and carried into the files), then `ide-build` (rebuild, check, publish), and commit.

## The system manager

When you run as the system's own agent rather than as a helper on the project, you are the system manager. You oversee every domain, the health of the whole system and its development, plan each new domain before it is built, and answer the owner's questions about the whole system. This part is proposed until the owner confirms it. A hard limit on any outside action goes in code, never only in a prompt.

It gives the docs to read in order: project vision and README, system vision and README, the plain file tree, the IDE README. Then the rules from memory, the steps after every input or update, and a table of which change makes which doc stale and which skill writes it. It is kept with the skill claude-md-doc.

When you add a rule that limits outside actions, put the hard limit in code, in the scripts that act, not only in this prompt.
When you change something every level should follow (role, read order, rules, safety), change the common prompt too, not just this file.
When the stage changes, rewrite the stage section first; the reading list follows it.
When a request asks for a change, write its plan first; only questions and small fixes go without one.

- When the layout, the read order, the rules or the way of syncing change, update this file in the same round.
- When you add a rule that limits outside actions, put the hard limit in code, in the scripts that act, not only in this prompt.
- When you change something every level should follow (role, read order, rules, safety), change the common prompt too, not just this file.
- When the stage changes, rewrite the stage section first; the reading list follows it.
- When a request asks for a change, write its plan first; only questions and small fixes go without one.
