| Keys and secrets | `.secrets/.secrets.index.md` | The keys folder and its files |
| Logs | `agents/system/logs/logs.index.md` | The shared logs for each source |
| Tests | `agents/system/tests/tests.index.md` | The structure of the tests of each level |
| Research | `agents/system/research/research.index.md` | The research list of the system |
| Self-improvement helpers | `agents/system/.claude/agents/sys-self-improvement-agent.index.md` | The self-improvement helper of the system |
| Each agent's AI setup | `agents/system/.claude/.claude.index.md` | The parts of an AI folder |
| The knowledge base and the docs | `agents/system/.claude/agents/knowledge-base-agent.md`, `vision/docs/README.md` | How the system keeps the knowledge and writes the documents |
| The project IDE | `apps/project-IDE/docs/README.md` | The File Tree page, and how the system builds, checks and publishes it |
| The server | `apps/project-IDE/docs/README.md` | The needs of the server, how to start it and get to it, and its settings |

## Still open in the design

These design subjects are not decided. The list shows them by part. The vision contains the questions about the goals and the business. The documents of each domain contain the open subjects of that domain.

**Agents and their levels**
- Does a small change make a new version of an agent? Examples are a new link, a changed job or a new model for one job.
- Can an agent change its own settings and documents? Or can only its self-improvement helper and its domain agent do this?

**The system agent and the shared files**
- Must the owner approve a change to the shared settings before the change gets to live agents?
- Must a file move automatically to the shared folders when a second agent needs it?

**Workers and data**
- How does an agent find the new data since its last run: with file times, or with a bookmark for each agent?
- Where are the workers helper and the helper that sets the limit of runs at the same time? What are their names?

**Jobs and the scheduler**
- Which computer runs the scheduler: the computer of the owner or a server that always operates?
- Does the scheduler make cloud jobs automatically, or does the owner approve each one?
- The global settings and the main run of an agent can both name important files. Which list has priority?
- The scheduler reads only jobs files. How do tests with their own schedules get to the scheduler?

**Links between agents**
- Does the repository keep the links, or does relink make them again after each download?
- Can an agent link each file of another agent, or only the files that the other agent lists as its output?

**Settings and AI models**
- What is the exact structure of the settings files? Which settings are shared?
- What are the exact default models: the thinking effort, the model for helpers, the other models?

**Keys and secrets**
- What keeps the list of keys the same as the key files?

**Logs**
- What is the exact log format? How long does the system keep logs?

**Tests**
- Does a failed test stop the runs of an agent, or only its move to live actions?

**Each agent's AI setup**
- Do the instructions of each level get the common base through a link, or as a copy when the system makes the agent?
- Do other levels keep their `CLAUDE.md` at the top of their folder, as the system does, or in `.claude/`?
- What does a version on Cursor use instead of `.claude/`?
- Which skills do all agents share? Can an agent get a shared skill as a link?

**The knowledge base and the docs**
- Where do the topic notes and the records go when the planning area `vision/` closes?
- Does a person write the lists of agents, workers and other items? Or does a script make them from one list that the screens of the owner also read?
- Must a check compare the tree notes with the real folders automatically?

**The project IDE**
- How does the server of the owner update the published page on claude.ai?

**The server**
- Who merges the changes from the two locations of the owner?

nodes.name: system.workers.json
nodes.summary: system's own jobs: when, where it runs, platform, model (D-029; was workers.config.json)
nodes.purpose: the system agent's own **jobs**: everything the system runs on a schedule or on demand, such as the data collectors shared by several domains [14.2], relinking and link checks, tests, index rebuilds and its sub-agent runs (SI [10.1.1.1]; the knowledge agent [10.1.1.2] as the `knowledge-sync` job, on changes under `agents/**` or `docs/inputs/**` and nightly, D-033). Every other agent has the same file for its own jobs in its `configs/` (domain [19.2.1], strategy [21.2.1], agent [27.4]), all in this format. The system sees each domain's file through [11.2] `subagents.link/` (D-030), and deeper ones one level down at a time.

details.label: All off for now (owner, page 2026-10-09, in-20261009-1040)
details.text: every system job has `enabled: false`; they stay in the file and run only once the owner turns them on.

details.label: What a job is (D-029)
details.text: either a plain **script** (`platform: none`) or an **AI run** on a coding-agent platform: the agent itself (`agent`: its main run, in its own folder), a `subagent`, a `skill`, a `workflow` or a slash `command`.

details.label: Job fields (proposed)
details.text: `id` (unique in the file) · `enabled` (turn off without deleting) · `purpose` · `type` (script | agent | subagent | skill | workflow | command) · `run` (the command for a script; the sub-agent, skill, workflow or command name otherwise) · `schedule` · `timezone` · `run_on` (local | cloud | desktop | github-actions) · `platform` (none | claude-code | cursor | codex) · `model` (`route` = take it from [11.11]) · `effort` · for AI runs: `prompt` (text, or `@path` to a prompt file), `workspace` (the folder it runs in; default the owner agent's folder), `allowed_tools`, `permission_mode`, `max_turns`, `max_cost_usd` · `secret_keys` (local runs only) · `inputs`, `outputs` · `on_change` (paths whose change starts the job; for the main run it cancels and restarts the current run) · `timeout`, `retries`, `concurrency` (skip | queue | restart) · `mode` (test | live; live needs owner approval) · `notify` (never | failure | always). The file's `defaults` fill in anything a job leaves out.

details.label: `schedule` (proposed, one short string)
details.text: `every 15m` / `every 6h` / `every 1d` · `cron 0 22 * * 1-5` · `once 2026-11-03 20:00` (runs one time, then shows as done) · `after [job-id]` (when that job succeeds) · `manual` (only from the UI or a command). Time zone from the job, else the file's `defaults`, else [11.1] `defaults.timezone`.

details.label: Where it runs (`run_on`, proposed)
details.text: `local` (default): headless on the machine that runs the scheduler [14.1], with the local files, links and test secrets. `cloud`: the platform's own cloud (Claude Code routines, Codex cloud, Cursor background agents): a fresh copy of the repo, no local files, no secrets; Claude Code routines run at most hourly. `desktop`: a Claude desktop scheduled task; it runs only while the app is open. `github-actions`: a scheduled workflow in the repo. The scheduler runs `local` jobs itself and registers the others on their platform.

details.label: How AI runs start (proposed)
details.text: `run-job` [14.1] builds the platform's headless command in the job's `workspace`: Claude Code `claude -p`, Cursor `cursor-agent -p`, Codex `codex exec`, with the job's model, prompt, tools, permission mode and turn limit. Adding a platform later means adding one command template to `run-job`.

details.label: Rules (proposed)
details.text: a `live` job needs owner approval and a live-allowed agent ([11.1] `modes`). `cloud`, `desktop` and `github-actions` jobs get no `secret_keys` and cannot act live. nodes.summary: system's own file links: what, from where (D-031; format for every level)
nodes.purpose: the system agent's own file links, and the **format every level uses**. Every agent has the same file in its `configs/`: domain [19.2.3], strategy [21.2.3], variant [27.3] (`[name]` as for the workers file: `system`, the domain name, or the agent name). For each link it says which file, from where, where it appears and why. The system's own list is short; most links sit in the agents at the lowest levels.

details.label: Fields (proposed)
details.text: `schema_version` · `agent` · `links[]`, one entry per link: `enabled` (off = relink removes the symlink but keeps the entry) · `to` (where the link appears, inside the agent's own `configs/`, `scripts/`, `logs/`, `data/`, `docs/`, `tests/` or `research/`; the name carries `.link`, e.g. `data/news-digest.link.md`) · `from` (the file it points at, see below) · `why` · `required` (true: a missing target is an error and the agent's main run does not start; false: a warning, and no link is made until the file exists) · `added_by` (create-agent, the agent itself, its SI sub-agent, owner) · `added` (date).

details.label: `from` (proposed)
details.text: a path under `agents/`, or a short form: `@system/…` (the system folder), `@domain/…` (the agent's own domain), `@strategy/…` (its own strategy, a level the prediction-market domain defines), `@[name]/…` (any domain or agent by its unique name, D-012, looked up in the registry [2.18.1], so the entry keeps working if that folder moves). Examples: `@system/data/subagents/news-digest/latest.md`, `@domain/data/markets-catalog/latest.json`, `@[other-domain]/data/[output]/latest.json` (another domain), `@[agent-name]/data/[output]/latest.json` (an agent anywhere, by its unique name).

details.label: Rules (proposed)
details.text: file links only (D-020): `from` is one real file; if it is itself a link, relink points at the real file behind it, so there are no chains. Never anything in `.secrets/` (D-023) or in any `.claude/` (D-030). `to` is always inside the agent's own folders, never inside `subagents.link/`. Links are relative symlinks and read-only for the agent. Child links (`subagents.link/`, D-030) are **not** listed here: relink builds them from the folder tree.

nodes.writers_readers: create-agent writes the first version; then the agent itself, its SI sub-agent and the owner (UI) edit it. `relink` and `check-links` [14.1] read it; the links index [16.1] and the UI show who links what.
open_questions: Commit the symlinks themselves to git (a fresh clone works at once; the pre-commit hook keeps them in step), or git-ignore them and let relink rebuild them after every clone and pull? Proposed: commit them. May an agent link any file of another agent, or only files that agent lists as `outputs` of its jobs (a public contract)?

- [14.1] `system/`: `*.system.js|py`, e.g. `create-agent` (**uniqueness check point for D-012**: validates the name format [2.7], rejects any name already in the registry [2.18.1] including retired ones, reserves the name, then scaffolds the folder and runs `init.sh`), `run-agent` (starts Claude Code in the agent's own folder (proposed, D-021), merges config, writes `effective-config.json`), `scheduler` (D-029; was `trigger-watcher`: finds every workers file by scanning `agents/**/configs/*.workers.json` (real files only, D-030), runs due jobs, watches `on_change` files with cancel-and-restart for main runs, registers cloud/desktop/GitHub jobs on their platform, keeps state in [16.1] `scheduler-state.json`, logs to [15.1]), `run-job` (D-029: runs one job: the script, or the platform's headless command in the job's workspace with its model, prompt and tools; passes only the job's `secret_keys` via `load-secret`; logs to the owner agent's `logs/jobs/[job-id]/`), `relink` (D-031: builds every link in the project from the links files ([11.13] format, found by scanning `agents/**/configs/*.links.json`, real files only) plus the child links from the folder tree (D-030): creates missing links, fixes changed ones, removes `.link` symlinks that no file lists, then runs the `check-links` rules; writes the links index [16.1] `links.index.json` (every link: owner agent, `to`, real target, required, status) and logs each change to [15.1]; re-runnable and safe at any time, one run at a time (lock). Options: `--agent [name]` (one agent; what `scripts/relink.system.link.js` presets when called from an agent folder), `--changed [files]` / `--staged` (works out which agents the changed files affect: a links file, an added, removed or moved agent folder, or a moved or deleted link target, using the links index), `--check` (report only; exit 1 if anything is wrong). **When it runs:** (1) a links file changes: the `relink` job in [11.10] watches `agents/**/configs/*.links.json` (`on_change`) and runs `--changed`, plus one full run a day; (2) review time: git hooks installed by the system `init.sh` [10.6]: `pre-commit` runs `--staged` and blocks the commit if a required link is broken, `post-merge` and `post-checkout` run `--changed` after a pull or branch switch, and the owner approving a change in the UI runs it too; (3) the agent itself: after editing its links file it runs `node scripts/relink.system.link.js` (rule in [2.17.3]), and a `PostToolUse` hook in its `.claude/settings.json` does it automatically ([2.7.2]); (4) `create-agent`, `init.sh` [40] and `stop-or-delete`), `check-links` (run by relink after every change and hourly on its own: broken links, cycles, symlinks without `.link` outside a `.link` folder, any `.claude` link (none for now, D-030), `subagents.link/` entries that are not a direct child's folder of the same kind, and any link or copy whose target is inside [47] `.secrets/` (D-023: never allowed)), `load-secret` (D-023, D-027: returns a key for the calling script at execution time, only if that agent's config lists it in `secret_keys` and, for `live/`, only if the owner approved the agent for live (in the prediction-market domain also with a funded, owner-approved account, [19.6.8]); returns the value to the process only, never to logs or the LLM), `notifier`, `run-tests` (D-025: runs a level's tests from its `tests.config.json` files, writes results back and to that level's `logs/tests.jsonl`; linked into each `tests/agents/` and `tests/scripts/` folder at every level as `run-tests.system.link.js`, which the level's links file lists, and into an agent's own `scripts/` (such as the trading agent's [30.2]) to run both kinds, which presets the kind and that folder's config; agent tests run Claude Code headless in test mode with no secrets, see [2.7.3]).
- [14.2] `workers/`: `*.worker.py|js`, data collectors shared by several domains; each runs as a job in [11.10] `system.workers.json` (D-029). A collector one domain needs lives in that domain (the Polymarket prices: [19.3.5], D-058).
- [14.3] `decisions/` moved to the prediction-market domain's `scripts/` (number kept, D-058).
- [14.4] `subagents.link/` (D-030): [14.4.1] `[domain-name]/` → that domain's `scripts/` [19.3].

# scripts/

## Summary

The shared scripts every agent uses, in JS/TS or Python, sorted by kind twice: by sub-folder and by the suffix `[name].[kind].[ext]`. The two general kinds are `system/`, the machinery (create-agent, run-agent, the scheduler and run-job, relink and check-links, load-secret, run-tests, notifier), and `workers/`, the data collectors shared by several domains. A domain keeps its own scripts and kinds, such as the prediction-market domain's `decisions/`, and the system reads them through `subagents.link/`. Agents use a shared script through a file link, so an improvement reaches every agent at once. System-support agents write here; domain and self-improvement agents propose.

## Keep in mind

- When you name a script, use `[name].[kind].[ext]` and put it in the sub-folder of its kind.
- When a second agent needs an agent-local script, move it to the shared `scripts/` of the nearest level both agents share (here when they are in different domains) and give each a file link; never copy it.
- When you add code here, give each runnable thing (function, endpoint, script, worker) its own file with one purpose; group related ones in a folder.

# docs/

## What it is

Trading's own docs, for people and for AI: `vision.md` (why trading has its own place and what every trading domain shares), `README.md` (every part of trading exactly, with each part's docs path), `README.asd.md` (the README again in ASD-STE100) and `rebuild-prompt.md` (how an AI builds `agents/trading/` again). Each doc has its How it works, Details, Example and Questions files next to it.

## Who looks after it

The knowledge base agent, with one skill per doc: `vision-doc`, `readme-doc`, the planned `readme-asd-doc` and `rebuild-prompt-doc`. The owner can change any doc on the File Tree page.

## When and how it changes

After an input or a decision that touches what every trading domain shares, the docs are rewritten in a fixed order: the vision, the README, its ASD-STE100 version, then the rebuild prompt. A change here then climbs to the system's docs above.

## Who uses it, and when

The owner and anyone new to trading, first; every trading domain agent as background; an AI rebuilding trading.

## Where it is mentioned

The system's README and rebuild prompt, the folder `agents/trading/`, and every trading domain's docs, which build on these.

## Related knowledge

They sit between the system's docs in `agents/system/docs/` and each trading domain's docs. The trading rules in full are in the kept trading notes in `vision/docs/prediction-market-agents/` until the prediction-market domain is written again in stage two.

## Keep in mind

- When you change one doc here, bring the others in line in the order vision, README, README.asd, rebuild prompt.
- When you write here, describe only what every trading domain shares.

nodes.content:
# Trading

## In short

Trading is the first kind of work the Agent OS does, and everything about it lives in one place: a folder of trading domains, with trading's own docs and its research. A trading domain is one area of trading, such as prediction markets. Every trading domain runs many small trading agents side by side, tries each idea in test mode with no real money, keeps the versions that work and lets only the owner put real money in. The first trading domain is prediction markets on Polymarket; a new one starts as a copy of it and changes only what is its own.

Where it stands: trading's docs and its research studies exist. The prediction-market domain exists only as its empty folders; its files are kept aside and it is written again in the project's second stage. Nothing that trades is built yet.

This document is the full, exact description of every part of `agents/trading/` and of what every trading domain holds, with the path to each part's own docs. It describes parts from the outside, never the logic inside an agent. Why trading has its own place, how it should work and its rules are in the vision, `agents/trading/docs/vision.md`.

## Trading at a glance

`agents/trading/` is a folder, not an agent. It has no AI instructions, no settings, no scripts and no jobs of its own, and no `.claude/` folder. Like every part of the Agent OS, each file and folder in it has a How it works file and a Details file next to it.

| Part | What it is for | Where it lives |
|---|---|---|
| Trading's docs | what every trading domain shares, how a new one is made, how to rebuild this folder | `agents/trading/docs/` |
| Research studies | the studies the trading domains start from | `agents/trading/researches/` |
| Prediction-market domain | the first trading domain, stage two, folders only today | `agents/trading/prediction-market/` |
| Later trading domains | copies of the prediction-market domain, made when the owner asks | `agents/trading/[domain]/`, none yet |
| Trading dashboard | the prediction-market domain's dashboard, empty | `apps/trading-ui/` |

How the parts connect:

1. The system agent reaches each trading domain directly, through its child links; this folder adds no level of agents between them.
2. A domain agent starts its strategies from the research studies here and from the owner's ideas.
3. Inside a domain, information flows down: workers collect prices and other data into the domain's `data/`, and each strategy and trading agent links the files it needs.
4. Trading agents write their decisions and orders to logs; their results flow up, level by level, to the domain agent and to the owner's dashboard.
5. The owner approves new trading agents and real money, and can stop any trading agent.

## How trading is laid out

```
agents/trading/
├── trading.index.md / trading.meta.json   How it works and Details of this folder
├── docs/                                  trading's own docs
│   ├── vision.md                          why trading, what every trading domain shares
│   ├── README.md                          this file
│   ├── README.asd.md                      this file again in ASD-STE100
│   └── rebuild-prompt.md                  how an AI rebuilds this folder
├── researches/                            the research studies
│   ├── prediction-market-research/        ways to make money on prediction markets
│   ├── self-improving-agents/             agents that improve themselves
│   └── trding-agents-arhiteches/          how trading agents are built
└── prediction-market/                     the first trading domain (stage two)
```

Every trading domain uses the standard agent folder at each of its three levels:

```
[agent folder]/
├── .claude/          the agent's AI setup: rules, skills, commands, sub-agents, workflows, output styles, memory
├── configs/          settings, jobs and links files, plus links to shared settings
├── scripts/          the agent's own scripts, plus links to shared ones
├── logs/             run logs and session logs
├── data/             what the agent's workers collect, plus links to shared data
├── docs/             vision.md, README.md, rebuild-prompt.md and the agent's notes
├── tests/            agents/ (tests of instructions) and scripts/ (tests of scripts)
├── research/         one folder per research item
└── [child agent]/    the agents one level down
```

A level with children has `subagents.link/` inside each content folder (`configs/`, `scripts/`, `logs/`, `data/`, `docs/`, `tests/`, `research/`), one folder link per child pointing at that child's folder of the same kind. A trading agent has no children and no `subagents.link/`.

## The parts

### Trading's docs

`agents/trading/docs/` holds trading's own docs for people and for AI: `vision.md` (why trading has its own place, what every trading domain shares, how a new one is made), this `README.md`, `README.asd.md` (this README in ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English, to compare with this one) and `rebuild-prompt.md` (the prompt an AI follows to rebuild this folder). Each doc has its How it works and Details files, an outline file (`[name].example.md`) and an open-questions file (`[name].questions.md`) next to it.

They sit between the system's docs above and each trading domain's docs below. They describe only what every trading domain shares; a single domain's detail stays in its own docs. When a trading domain changes in a way that touches what all domains share, these docs are brought in line, and then the system's docs above them.

The knowledge base agent writes them with the `vision-doc`, `readme-doc`, `readme-asd-doc` (planned) and `rebuild-prompt-doc` skills; the owner can change them on the File Tree page.

Its docs: `agents/trading/docs/docs.index.md`

### Research studies

`agents/trading/researches/` holds the research studies, real files that were here before any trading agent. The folder keeps the owner's name `researches/`; every agent's own research history lives in its `research/` folder instead.

- `prediction-market-research/`: forty-two studies of ways to make money on prediction markets, numbered `01` to `34` and `50` to `57`, one Markdown file each, such as `01-maker-reward-pool-farming.md` and `21-llm-forecasting-agents.md`. Some describe practices to avoid, such as wash trading and insider trading. `_evidence/` holds the background evidence (`E1` to `E9`: venue mechanics, incentive programs, resolution, profitability, other venues, tooling, AI forecasting, multi-agent simulation, legal) with the strategy lists and one row per study; `_pipeline/` holds the pipeline that wrote the studies.
- `self-improving-agents/`: one study of approaches and architectures for agents that improve themselves.
- `trding-agents-arhiteches/`: a study of how trading agents are built: `README.md`, twenty-nine architecture specs in `specs/`, their diagrams in `diagrams/` and a gallery page `index.html`.

The domain agents read these studies when they look for strategies; the owner reads them on the File Tree page. A study is not changed after the fact; when it leads to a decision, the decision is recorded in the notes.

Its docs: `agents/trading/researches/researches.index.md`

### The trading domains

Each trading domain is a full domain of the Agent OS, in its own folder under `agents/trading/`, and a direct child of the system agent. Each arranges its agents in three levels, each with the standard agent folder:

- **The domain agent**, in the domain's folder: finds, creates and updates strategies, makes sure the domain makes money, answers the owner's questions.
- **Strategy agents**, one folder each inside the domain, such as `strategy-1-agent/`: each owns one way to make money, its definition and its versions.
- **Trading agents** (variants), one folder each inside their strategy: the versions that actually trade.

**The prediction-market domain** (`agents/trading/prediction-market/`) is the first. It trades on Polymarket first. Today it holds only its folders, each with a `.gitkeep`: the standard folder of the domain (with `scripts/decisions/`, `logs/jobs/`, `logs/services/`, `data/markets-catalog/`, `data/polymarket-prices/`, `docs/common/`, `docs/how-to/` and `docs/index/` inside), one strategy `strategy-1-agent/`, and one example trading agent below it, `pm-strategy-1.momentum-v1.opus55-test/`, where "momentum" is only a placeholder. Its earlier files are kept in `vision/archive/2026-10-12/prediction-market/` and its trading notes in `vision/docs/prediction-market-agents/`; in the second stage the domain is written again from them, with its own vision, README and rebuild prompt.

**Later trading domains**, such as copy trading, are copies of the prediction-market domain, made when the owner asks. None is in the tree.

Its docs: `agents/trading/prediction-market/docs/`, empty until the second stage brings its `README.md`

### What every trading domain holds

Every trading domain has the same kinds of trading parts, in its own standard folder. The prediction-market domain defines them first and a copied domain keeps their shape:

- **The domain's trading settings**, one file in its `configs/`: risk limits for the whole domain, per agent and per venue; the trading accounts; the venues, fees and market filters; the currency; the order stop switch; and which trade alerts reach the owner. In the prediction-market domain it is `prediction-market-agents.config.json`. Trading agents reach it through a file link and may only make its limits tighter (our proposal).
- **The shared trading scripts**, in `scripts/decisions/`: the scripts that buy, sell and check risk, named `[name].decision.[ext]`. `decision` is a script kind the trading domains add to the system's `worker` and `system` kinds. Every order goes through a decision script, which reads the mode and the limits before it acts. Trading agents link the ones they need.
- **The order logs**, in `logs/services/[service]/`: every order, test or live, logged by the service that placed it.
- **The trading notes**, in `docs/`: the trading layer of the system's notes, each named with a `trading-` prefix (overview, architecture, conventions, safety, data formats, flows, metrics, glossary, roadmap, feature map), plus `common/` (the trading agent's design, the trading prompt, the strategy self-improvement templates), `how-to/` (go live with money, add a trading account, stop a trading agent, create a strategy or variant) and `index/` (the list of trading accounts). A domain also keeps `doc-outlines.md`, which says what the docs of each of its levels hold.

Its docs: each trading domain's own `docs/README.md`

### Names of strategies and trading agents

A trading agent's name starts with its strategy and ends with its AI model and its mode: `[strategy-id].[own-name]-v[N].[platform-model]-[test|live]`, for example `pm-strategy-1.momentum-v1.opus55-test`. The folder of a trading agent is named after it. A strategy agent's ID carries its main model and mode too, such as `pm-strategy-1-agent.opus55-test`, while its folder keeps a plain name such as `strategy-1-agent/`. Names are lowercase letters, digits, `-` and `.`, at most 64 characters. The rule that the name starts with the strategy is decided; the exact format is our proposal.

A changed setting, instruction or script makes a new trading agent and raises `v[N]`; a different model changes the model part. Names are never changed or reused, because test and live versions are different agents.

Its docs: `vision/docs/prediction-market-agents/trading-conventions.md` until the domain's notes are written again

### Accounts, keys and real money

A trading account is an account or wallet at a venue that a trading agent may use. Accounts are listed in the domain's trading settings, each with its id, venue, mode, whether it is funded, whether the owner approved it, the agent it is assigned to, its maximum capital and the names of its keys; the domain's `docs/index/` keeps a readable list of them.

Keys are kept like every key in the Agent OS: values only in the git-ignored `.env` files in `.secrets/test/` and `.secrets/live/`, known everywhere else by name only, with a prefix per account such as `POLYMARKET_ACCT1_API_KEY`. The system's `load-secret` script hands an account's keys to one process at a time and refuses live keys unless the owner approved the account.

Only the owner approves an account with real money, adds its live keys and changes the risk limits or the accounts. No agent approves an account, for itself or for another.

Its docs: `vision/docs/prediction-market-agents/trading-safety.md` until the domain's notes are written again

### Test and live

Every trading agent starts in test mode, including every version made by self-improvement. In test, orders are simulated at the price seen at decision time, or placed on a test network on blockchains. A trading agent goes live only when the owner has approved it and given it a funded, approved account. Every new strategy configuration starts only after the owner has read a report on it and approved it.

For now orders are placed only on blockchains, on any network and app; centralised exchanges and other apps are sources of information only. Every decision script checks the system's general stop switch and the domain's order stop switch before every order, in test and in live; both stop switches are our proposal, and what the order stop switch does with open positions is still open.

Its docs: `vision/docs/prediction-market-agents/how-to/go-live-with-money.md` until the domain's notes are written again

### Metrics and comparing versions

Trading agents are measured on money, on top of the system's cost, speed and error measures. We propose: realised and unrealised profit and loss and the return on capital, all from the order logs; win rate with its number of trades; the largest and the current fall from a peak; calibration, comparing the agent's forecasts with what happened and with the market price; and AI cost per trade. Versions of one strategy are compared over the same period and capital, in test against test. Which numbers decide success is still open.

Its docs: `vision/docs/prediction-market-agents/trading-metrics.md` until the domain's notes are written again

### Making a new trading domain

A new trading domain is a copy of the prediction-market domain, made when the owner asks. The system's `create-agent` script creates its domain agent and folders, never a copy by hand. The copy keeps the levels, the standard folders, the trading notes, the shape of the trading settings and the decision scripts, and changes what is its own: venues, fees, market filters, information sources, strategies and risk limits. It starts with no funded account. When two domains need the same trading part, that part can move up into `agents/trading/`; until then it stays in the domain.

Its docs: `agents/trading/docs/rebuild-prompt.md`

### The trading dashboard

`apps/trading-ui/` is planned as the prediction-market domain's dashboard: a page where the owner sees every trading agent and its results, approves real money, and stops or deletes agents. It stays in `apps/` and is empty for now; whether it is needed at all is still open.

Its docs: `apps/trading-ui/trading-ui.index.md`

## Where each part's docs are

| Part | Its docs | What they add |
|---|---|---|
| Trading's folder | `agents/trading/trading.index.md` | how the folder works, in short |
| Trading's docs | `agents/trading/docs/docs.index.md` | what each doc is for |
| Research studies | `agents/trading/researches/researches.index.md` | the studies and how they are used |
| Prediction-market domain | `agents/trading/prediction-market/docs/` | empty today; its vision, README and rebuild prompt in stage two |
| Trading notes (kept) | `vision/docs/prediction-market-agents/` | the trading rules, formats, flows and metrics in full |
| Trading dashboard | `apps/trading-ui/trading-ui.index.md` | the planned dashboard |
| The system above | `agents/system/docs/README.md` | everything every agent shares |

## Still open in the design

- **Trading folder:** which parts move up into `agents/trading/` once there are two trading domains.
- **Domains:** which trading domain comes next and when; copy trading is the likely one.
- **Names:** whether `v[N]` belongs to the trading agent or to the strategy; whether strategy folders carry the model and mode too; the shorter form `strategy-1/strategy-1.v1.Claude-Opus5.5/` that has come up for folder names.
- **Safety:** what the order stop switch does with open positions; the capital limits of the first live accounts; how account entries map to key prefixes.
- **Metrics:** which numbers decide success; where positions are kept; where market outcomes are recorded.
- **Self-improvement:** whether a strategy may fold a winning change into itself, or retire losing versions, without the owner.
- **Owner:** the channel for trade alerts.

## Who looks after it

The knowledge base agent writes it with the `readme-doc` skill, after the vision and before the ASD-STE100 version and the rebuild prompt. The owner can also change it on the File Tree page.

## When and how it changes

It changes after every change to a part of trading: a new or removed trading domain, a new study in the research folder, a settled design point, a change to names, accounts, test and live or metrics. nodes.questions_md:
# README.md: open questions

- **Which shared trading parts move up into `agents/trading/` once there are two trading domains?** The README describes the settings, decision scripts and notes as living in a domain; a move would change the layout and several parts.
- **Is `v[N]` part of the trading agent's name or of the strategy's?** It changes the names in "Names of strategies and trading agents" and every example path.
- **Do strategy folders carry the model and mode, or do folders take the shorter form `strategy-1/strategy-1.v1.Claude-Opus5.5/`?** Renaming touches every path under the prediction-market domain.
- **Is `apps/trading-ui/` still needed, or does the project IDE take its place?** The README lists it as the planned dashboard.
- **Where are positions kept, and where are market outcomes recorded?** The metrics part depends on both.
- **How do account entries map to key prefixes in the `.env` files?** The accounts part names the prefix rule but not the mapping.

# Trading (ASD-STE100)

This file is the ASD-STE100 version of `README.md` in this folder. `README.md` is the source. If the two files do not agree, use `README.md`.

## In short

Trading is the first type of work in the Agent OS. All of the trading work is in one folder. This folder contains the trading domains, the trading docs and the trading research.

A trading domain is one area of trading, for example prediction markets. Each trading domain operates many small trading agents at the same time. Each idea starts in test mode, with no real money. The system keeps the versions that work. Only the owner can give real money to an agent.

The first trading domain is prediction markets on Polymarket. A new trading domain starts as a copy of the prediction-market domain. Then it changes only its own parts.

Status: the trading docs and the research studies exist. The prediction-market domain has only empty folders. Its old files are in an archive. The project writes this domain again in stage two. No part that trades exists at this time.

This document gives a full and exact description of each part of `agents/trading/`. It also tells what each trading domain contains, and where the docs of each part are. It does not tell how an agent makes decisions. The vision, `agents/trading/docs/vision.md`, tells why trading has its own folder, how trading must operate and the rules.

## Trading at a glance

`agents/trading/` is a folder. It is not an agent. It has no AI instructions, no settings, no scripts and no jobs. It has no `.claude/` folder. Each file and each folder in it has a How it works file and a Details file.

| Part | Purpose | Location |
|---|---|---|
| Trading's docs | Tell what all trading domains share, how to make a new domain and how to build this folder again | `agents/trading/docs/` |
| Research studies | Give the start information for the trading domains | `agents/trading/researches/` |
| Prediction-market domain | The first trading domain. Stage two. Folders only at this time | `agents/trading/prediction-market/` |
| Later trading domains | Copies of the prediction-market domain. The owner asks for them | `agents/trading/[domain]/`. None at this time |
| Trading dashboard | The dashboard of the prediction-market domain. Empty | `apps/trading-ui/` |

How the parts connect:

1. The system agent connects to each trading domain directly, through its child links. This folder does not add a level of agents.
2. A domain agent uses the research studies and the ideas of the owner to start its strategies.
3. In a domain, information goes down. Workers collect prices and other data into the `data/` folder of the domain. Each strategy and each trading agent links the files that it needs.
4. Trading agents write their decisions and orders to logs. Their results go up, level by level, to the domain agent and to the dashboard of the owner.
5. The owner approves new trading agents and real money. The owner can stop each trading agent.

## How trading is laid out

```
agents/trading/
├── trading.index.md / trading.meta.json   How it works and Details of this folder
├── docs/                                  trading's own docs
│   ├── vision.md                          why trading, what all trading domains share
│   ├── README.md                          the source of this file
│   ├── README.asd.md                      this file
│   └── rebuild-prompt.md                  how an AI builds this folder again
├── researches/                            the research studies
│   ├── prediction-market-research/        ways to make money on prediction markets
│   ├── self-improving-agents/             agents that make themselves better
│   └── trding-agents-arhiteches/          how trading agents are built
└── prediction-market/                     the first trading domain (stage two)
```

Each trading domain uses the standard agent folder at each of its three levels:

```
[agent folder]/
├── .claude/          the AI setup of the agent: rules, skills, commands, sub-agents, workflows, output styles, memory
├── configs/          settings, jobs and links files, and links to shared settings
├── scripts/          the scripts of the agent, and links to shared scripts
├── logs/             run logs and session logs
├── data/             the data that the workers of the agent collect, and links to shared data
├── docs/             vision.md, README.md, rebuild-prompt.md and the notes of the agent
├── tests/            agents/ (tests of instructions) and scripts/ (tests of scripts)
├── research/         one folder for each research item
└── [child agent]/    the agents one level below
```

A level with children has a `subagents.link/` folder in each content folder. The content folders are `configs/`, `scripts/`, `logs/`, `data/`, `docs/`, `tests/` and `research/`. `subagents.link/` contains one folder link for each child. Each link goes to the folder of the same type in that child. A trading agent has no children. Thus it has no `subagents.link/` folder.

## The parts

### Trading's docs

`agents/trading/docs/` contains the trading docs. People and AI read them. The docs are:

- `vision.md`: why trading has its own folder, what all trading domains share and how to make a new domain.
- `README.md`: the full description of the parts.
- `README.asd.md`: this file. It is `README.md` in ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English. Use it to compare the two texts.
- `rebuild-prompt.md`: the prompt that an AI uses to build this folder again.

Each doc has a How it works file and a Details file. Each doc also has an outline file (`[name].example.md`) and a file of open questions (`[name].questions.md`).

These docs are between the system docs above and the docs of each trading domain below. They tell only what all trading domains share. The details of one domain stay in the docs of that domain. If a change in a domain affects all domains, update these docs. Then update the system docs above them.

The knowledge base agent writes these docs. It uses the skills `vision-doc`, `readme-doc`, `readme-asd-doc` (planned) and `rebuild-prompt-doc`. The owner can also change the docs on the File Tree page.

Its docs: `agents/trading/docs/docs.index.md`

### Research studies

`agents/trading/researches/` contains the research studies. These are real files. They existed before the trading agents. The folder keeps the name `researches/` that the owner gave it. The research history of each agent is in the `research/` folder of that agent.

- `prediction-market-research/`: 42 studies of ways to make money on prediction markets. The numbers are `01` to `34` and `50` to `57`. Each study is one Markdown file, for example `01-maker-reward-pool-farming.md`. Some studies describe practices that you must not do, for example wash trading and insider trading. `_evidence/` contains the background evidence `E1` to `E9`, the strategy lists and one row for each study. `_pipeline/` contains the pipeline that wrote the studies.
- `self-improving-agents/`: one study of methods and architectures for agents that make themselves better.
- `trding-agents-arhiteches/`: one study of how trading agents are built. It contains `README.md`, 29 architecture specifications in `specs/`, their diagrams in `diagrams/` and a gallery page `index.html`.

The domain agents read these studies when they look for strategies. The owner reads them on the File Tree page. Do not change a study after it is complete. If a study causes a decision, record the decision in the notes.

Its docs: `agents/trading/researches/researches.index.md`

### The trading domains

Each trading domain is a full domain of the Agent OS. Each domain has its own folder in `agents/trading/`. Each domain is a direct child of the system agent. Each domain has three levels of agents. Each level uses the standard agent folder:

- **The domain agent** is in the folder of the domain. It finds, makes and updates strategies. It makes sure that the domain makes money. It answers the questions of the owner.
- **Strategy agents** each have one folder in the domain, for example `strategy-1-agent/`. Each strategy agent owns one way to make money, its definition and its versions.
- **Trading agents** (variants) each have one folder in their strategy. They are the versions that trade.

**The prediction-market domain** (`agents/trading/prediction-market/`) is the first domain. It trades on Polymarket first. At this time it contains only folders. Each folder contains a `.gitkeep` file. The folders are:

- the standard folder of the domain, with `scripts/decisions/`, `logs/jobs/`, `logs/services/`, `data/markets-catalog/`, `data/polymarket-prices/`, `docs/common/`, `docs/how-to/` and `docs/index/`;
- one strategy, `strategy-1-agent/`;
- one example trading agent below the strategy, `pm-strategy-1.momentum-v1.opus55-test/`. The word "momentum" is only a placeholder.

The old files of the domain are in `vision/archive/2026-10-12/prediction-market/`. Its trading notes are in `vision/docs/prediction-market-agents/`. In stage two, the project writes the domain again from these files. The domain then gets its own vision, README and rebuild prompt.

**Later trading domains** are copies of the prediction-market domain, for example copy trading. The owner asks for them. At this time, none is in the tree.

Its docs: `agents/trading/prediction-market/docs/`. This folder is empty until stage two adds its `README.md`.

### What every trading domain holds

Each trading domain has the same types of trading parts in its standard folder. The prediction-market domain defines them first. A copied domain keeps their shape.

- **The trading settings of the domain** are one file in its `configs/` folder. This file contains:
  - risk limits for the full domain, for each agent and for each venue;
  - the trading accounts;
  - the venues, fees and market filters;
  - the currency;
  - the order stop switch;
  - the trade alerts that go to the owner.

  In the prediction-market domain, the file is `prediction-market-agents.config.json`. Trading agents connect to it through a file link. A trading agent can only make the limits tighter (proposal).
- **The shared trading scripts** are in `scripts/decisions/`. These scripts buy, sell and check risk. Their names are `[name].decision.[ext]`. The trading domains add the script type `decision` to the system types `worker` and `system`. Each order goes through a decision script. The decision script reads the mode and the limits before it does an action. Trading agents link the scripts that they need.
- **The order logs** are in `logs/services/[service]/`. The service that places an order logs it. This is true for test orders and live orders.
- **The trading notes** are in `docs/`. They are the trading layer of the system notes. Each name starts with `trading-`. The notes are overview, architecture, conventions, safety, data formats, flows, metrics, glossary, roadmap and feature map. Other folders are:
  - `common/`: the design of the trading agent, the trading prompt and the strategy self-improvement templates;
  - `how-to/`: go live with money, add a trading account, stop a trading agent, make a strategy or a variant;
  - `index/`: the list of trading accounts.

  A domain also keeps `doc-outlines.md`. This file tells what the docs of each level contain.

Its docs: the `docs/README.md` file of each trading domain

### Names of strategies and trading agents

The name of a trading agent starts with its strategy. The name ends with its AI model and its mode. The format is `[strategy-id].[own-name]-v[N].[platform-model]-[test|live]`. An example is `pm-strategy-1.momentum-v1.opus55-test`. The folder of a trading agent has the same name as the agent.

The ID of a strategy agent also contains its main model and its mode, for example `pm-strategy-1-agent.opus55-test`. The folder of the strategy keeps a simple name, for example `strategy-1-agent/`.

Names use only lowercase letters, digits, `-` and `.`. The maximum length is 64 characters. The owner decided that the name starts with the strategy. The exact format is a proposal.

A changed setting, instruction or script makes a new trading agent. Then `v[N]` increases by one. A different model changes the model part of the name. Do not change or use again a name. A test version and a live version are different agents.

Its docs: `vision/docs/prediction-market-agents/trading-conventions.md`, until the project writes the domain notes again

### Accounts, keys and real money

A trading account is an account or a wallet at a venue. A trading agent can use it. The trading settings of the domain list the accounts. Each account entry has these data:

- its ID and its venue;
- its mode;
- funded or not funded;
- approved by the owner or not approved;
- the agent that uses it;
- its maximum capital;
- the names of its keys.

The `docs/index/` folder of the domain keeps a list of the accounts that people can read.

Keys follow the key rules of the Agent OS. The key values are only in the `.env` files in `.secrets/test/` and `.secrets/live/`. Git does not keep these files. All other files use only the key names. Each key name has a prefix for its account, for example `POLYMARKET_ACCT1_API_KEY`. The system script `load-secret` gives the keys of an account to one process at a time. It refuses live keys if the owner did not approve the account.

Only the owner can:

- approve an account with real money;
- add its live keys;
- change the risk limits or the accounts.

An agent cannot approve an account. This is true for itself and for other agents.

Its docs: `vision/docs/prediction-market-agents/trading-safety.md`, until the project writes the domain notes again

### Test and live

Each trading agent starts in test mode. This is also true for each version that self-improvement makes. In test mode, the system simulates each order at the price at the time of the decision. On blockchains, test mode can also use a test network.

A trading agent goes live only when the owner approves it. The owner must also give it a funded and approved account. A new strategy configuration starts only after the owner reads a report on it and approves it.

At this time, agents place orders only on blockchains. They can use all networks and apps. Centralised exchanges and other apps are only sources of information.

Each decision script checks two stop switches before each order: the general stop switch of the system and the order stop switch of the domain. It does this in test mode and in live mode. The two stop switches are proposals. The effect of the order stop switch on open positions is an open question.

Its docs: `vision/docs/prediction-market-agents/how-to/go-live-with-money.md`, until the project writes the domain notes again

### Metrics and comparing versions

The system measures trading agents on money. It also uses the cost, speed and error measures of the system. We propose these measures:

- realised profit and loss, unrealised profit and loss, and the return on capital, from the order logs;
- win rate, with the number of trades;
- the largest fall from a peak and the current fall from a peak;
- calibration: the forecasts of the agent compared with the results and with the market price;
- AI cost for each trade.

The system compares the versions of one strategy over the same period and the same capital. It compares test results with test results. The measures that decide success are an open question.

Its docs: `vision/docs/prediction-market-agents/trading-metrics.md`, until the project writes the domain notes again

### Making a new trading domain

A new trading domain is a copy of the prediction-market domain. The owner asks for it. Do these steps:

1. Use the system script `create-agent` to make the domain agent and its folders. Do not copy the folders by hand.
2. Keep the levels, the standard folders, the trading notes, the shape of the trading settings and the decision scripts.
3. Change the parts of the new domain: venues, fees, market filters, information sources, strategies and risk limits.
4. Start the domain with no funded account.

If two domains need the same trading part, move that part up into `agents/trading/`. Until then, keep it in the domain.

Its docs: `agents/trading/docs/rebuild-prompt.md`

### The trading dashboard

`apps/trading-ui/` is the planned dashboard of the prediction-market domain. On this page, the owner sees each trading agent and its results. The owner approves real money there, and stops or deletes agents. The folder stays in `apps/`. It is empty at this time. It is an open question if the project needs it.

Its docs: `apps/trading-ui/trading-ui.index.md`

## Where each part's docs are

| Part | Its docs | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| Trading's folder | `agents/trading/trading.index.md` | a short description of the folder |
| Trading's docs | `agents/trading/docs/docs.index.md` | the purpose of each doc |
| Research studies | `agents/trading/researches/researches.index.md` | the studies and how agents use them |
| Prediction-market domain | `agents/trading/prediction-market/docs/` | empty at this time. Its vision, README and rebuild prompt come in stage two |
| Trading notes (kept) | `vision/docs/prediction-market-agents/` | all the trading rules, formats, flows and metrics |
| Trading dashboard | `apps/trading-ui/trading-ui.index.md` | the planned dashboard |
| The system above | `agents/system/docs/README.md` | all the parts that all agents share |

## Still open in the design

- **Trading folder:** Which parts go up into `agents/trading/` when there are two trading domains?
- **Domains:** Which trading domain is next, and when? Copy trading is the probable next domain.
- **Names:** Is `v[N]` part of the trading agent or part of the strategy? Do strategy folders also contain the model and the mode? Do folders use the shorter form `strategy-1/strategy-1.v1.Claude-Opus5.5/`?
- **Safety:** What does the order stop switch do with open positions? What are the capital limits of the first live accounts? How do account entries connect to key prefixes?
- **Metrics:** Which measures decide success? Where does the system keep positions? Where does the system record market results?
- **Self-improvement:** Can a strategy put a winning change into itself without the owner? Can it stop losing versions without the owner?
- **Owner:** Which channel sends trade alerts to the owner?

nodes.content:
# Trading in the Agent OS: vision

## In short

Trading is the first kind of work the Agent OS does, and everything about it lives in one place: a folder of trading domains, with trading's own docs and its research. A trading domain is one area of trading, such as prediction markets, where people trade on the outcome of events. Every trading domain runs many small trading agents side by side, tries each idea in test mode with no real money, keeps the versions that work and lets only the owner put real money in. The first trading domain is prediction markets on Polymarket; a new one starts as a copy of it and changes only what is its own. Today trading has its docs and its research, and the prediction-market domain is a set of empty folders waiting for the project's second stage.

## Why trading has its own place

The Agent OS runs agents of any kind, and its top level says only what holds for all of them. Trading brings much that other kinds of work do not share: money, trading accounts, markets, orders, fees, risk limits and trade alerts. Keeping all of it in one place keeps the rest of the system general and gives every trading domain one home for what trading means.

There are also many ways to make money by trading, and most first ideas fail. On prediction markets alone there are up to about eighty approaches; crypto, following traders who already do well and trading on what one well-known person says bring their own. One home lets these domains grow side by side, learn from each other and later be combined.

The goals: agents that make money cheaply in ways that are simple to understand; every idea tried in test first; real money always under the owner's control; and results compared fairly, so the better versions win.

## The concept

Trading is a folder, not an agent: it has no instructions, settings or jobs of its own. It holds trading's own docs, the research studies the trading domains start from, and the trading domains themselves.

Each trading domain is a full domain of the Agent OS and arranges its agents in three levels:

- **The domain agent** owns the area: it finds and creates strategies, makes sure the domain makes money and answers the owner's questions.
- **Strategy agents**, one per way to make money. A strategy can be plain code, AI or a mix, and may have its own way of testing on past data.
- **Trading agents**, also called variants: the versions of a strategy that actually trade, each with one set of changes, one AI model and one mode, test or live. A trading agent's name starts with its strategy and ends with its model and mode, so its versions sort together and can be compared.

Every agent has the same standard folder: settings, scripts, logs, data, docs, tests, research and its own AI setup, and a parent reaches its children's folders one level at a time.

What only one trading domain uses stays in that domain: its trading notes, its settings with risk limits and accounts, and its shared buy, sell and risk scripts. When a second domain needs the same thing, that part can move up into trading's own folder.

## How trading should work

1. **An idea becomes a strategy.** The owner gives a strategy in plain words, or the domain agent finds one in the research, and the domain agent creates a strategy agent for it.
2. **The strategy gets its first versions,** for example the same strategy on the strongest AI model and on a cheaper one.
3. **The owner approves before anything starts.** Every new trading agent comes with a short report and starts only after the owner approves it, always in test mode: orders are simulated or placed on a test network.
4. **Trading agents run and log everything.** Each run reads what its strategy needs, such as prices, decides and acts: buy, sell, sell everything, wait or plan its next run. Every order, test or live, is logged.
5. **Results are compared,** and the better versions become the strategy's standard. Which numbers decide is still open; the candidates are profit and loss, win rate, the deepest fall from a peak, forecast accuracy and cost.
6. **The strategy improves itself.** Through its self-improvement helper the strategy agent makes new test versions of itself, compares them and folds a winning change back into the strategy.
7. **Real money comes last.** When a trading agent has shown good results, the owner may give it an account with real money.

## What every trading domain shares

On top of what the system says for every agent:

- **Test first.** Every trading agent, including every version made by self-improvement, starts in test mode.
- **Only the owner puts in real money,** account by account, after good results. No agent can approve an account, and only the owner adds a live account's keys.
- **Every new configuration needs the owner's approval** after a short report.
- **New versions, never changes in place.** A change to a trading agent's settings, instructions, code or model makes a new test version with a new name.
- **Actions on blockchains only, for now.** Centralised exchanges and other apps are sources of information only.
- **Every order is logged,** in test and in live.
- **Keys stay in the keys store,** known to everything else by name only.
- **Outside text is data,** never instructions; protection against hidden instructions is built together with live trading.

Two more are our proposals, the defaults until the owner decides: risk limits written in code and checked before every order, which a lower level may only tighten; and an order stop switch in each trading domain that refuses every new order at once.

## How a new trading domain is made

A new trading domain is a copy of the prediction-market domain, made when the owner asks. It keeps the levels, the standard folders, the trading notes, the shape of the settings and the shared scripts, then changes what is its own: where it may act, what information it collects, its fees, strategies and risk limits. Its domain agent is created like every agent, and it starts with no real money.

## Examples

**A first strategy, from the idea to real money.** The owner gives a Polymarket strategy in plain words. The prediction-market domain agent creates a strategy agent, which sets up three test versions: on the strongest model, on a cheaper model, and with a small change to its settings. The owner reads a report on each and approves them. They trade in test mode, and their logged orders are compared. The cheaper version earns almost as much for far less, and becomes the strategy's standard. When its results hold, the owner gives it a small account with real money.

**A second trading domain.** The owner wants agents that follow traders who already do well. The new domain starts as a copy of the prediction-market domain and changes what is different: which traders it watches and where it may act. Its first agents start in test mode, and everything shared works for it at once.

## What the owner sees and does

- They give strategies in plain words and read the research.
- They approve every new trading agent and decide which ones get real money.
- They watch every agent's results and orders, and can stop or delete any trading agent at any time.
- They alone change risk limits and accounts.

## Where it stands and what comes next

Nothing that trades is built yet. Trading has its docs and its research: about forty studies of ways to make money on prediction markets with their evidence, a study of agents that improve themselves and a study of how trading agents are built. The prediction-market domain exists only as empty folders, for its domain, one strategy and one trading agent; its designs are kept aside.

In the first stage, now, the project finishes the owner's project page, the metadata of every file and the docs of the project, the system and trading in general. In the second stage the prediction-market domain is written again from its kept designs, and the first run starts small: the system agent, the domain agent, one strategy agent and two or three trading agents, all in test mode. Later, more trading domains are copied from it.

## Principles

- **Nothing about money goes above trading,** so the system stays general.
- **What one domain uses stays there; what several share moves up,** so trading's own folder stays small until sharing is real.
- **The owner approves real money, every time,** because it is the one thing no agent may decide.
- **An AI may propose a trade; code checks the limits,** so a mistaken or tricked AI cannot break them. This is our proposal.

## Ideas we are still weighing

**One part that places every order.** If every agent places its own orders, a bug in one can skip a limit. Instead, agents would only write the orders they want, and one shared part would check the limits and place them. All money checks would sit in one place.

**One ledger for positions and cash.** If each agent keeps its own record of what it holds, records can disagree with the account. One ledger, written only by the part that places orders, would give one true answer to what is held.

**Champion and challengers.** A version that changes itself while trading can drift unnoticed. Instead, each new version would have to beat the current best in test, over the same period, before it takes its place.

## Open questions

- **How is success measured?** It sets what self-improvement aims for.
- **How much money goes live first?** It sets how much a mistake can cost.
- **What happens to open positions when trading is stopped?** Closing them needs orders while the stop refuses new ones.
- **May a strategy fold a winning change into itself without the owner?** It decides how fast strategies improve and how much the owner reviews.
- **Which trading domain comes next, and when?** Copy trading is the likely one.
- **How are trading agents named on disk?** A shorter form with the model's full name has come up next to the names in use.
- **How does the owner get trade alerts?** The channel is not chosen yet.

## Going deeper

The README describes every part of trading exactly: its folders, its research, what every trading domain holds and where each part's docs are, at `agents/trading/docs/README.md`.

# vision.md: open questions

- **Which numbers decide success for a trading agent?** Profit and loss, win rate, the deepest fall from a peak, calibration and cost are the candidates. The answer sets what self-improvement aims for and when a version wins.
- **What are the capital limits for the first live accounts?** They set how much a mistake can cost when real money starts.
- **What does the order stop switch do with open positions?** Closing positions needs orders while the switch refuses new ones; the vision cannot state the stop rule until this is settled.
- **May a strategy fold a winning change into itself, or retire losing versions, without the owner?** It decides how fast strategies improve and how much the owner reviews.
- **Which trading domain comes next, and when?** Copy trading was named as the next domain; the vision lists it only as an example until the owner asks for it.
- **How should trading agents and strategies be named on disk?** The names in use are `strategy-1-agent/pm-strategy-1.momentum-v1.opus55-test/`; the stage-one request wrote `strategy-1/strategy-1.v1.Claude-Opus5.5/`. The vision describes the current form until the owner chooses.
- **Through which channel does the owner get trade alerts?** The vision says alerts exist but not how they arrive.
- **Should the order executor and the single ledger become part of the design?** Both are listed as ideas being weighed.

# Rebuild trading: `agents/trading/`

## Your task

You are an AI coding agent, such as Claude Code, working in the Agent OS repository. The system is already built from its own prompt, `agents/system/docs/rebuild-prompt.md`: the top of the tree, `agents/system/`, `.secrets/`, the shared scripts, the skills and the project IDE in `apps/project-IDE/`. Your job is to build `agents/trading/` and its docs, and nothing else.

You build:

1. the folder `agents/trading/` with its How it works and Details files;
2. trading's docs in `agents/trading/docs/`: `vision.md`, `README.md`, `README.asd.md`, `rebuild-prompt.md` (this file), each with its metadata files;
3. the research folder `agents/trading/researches/`, restored as it is;
4. the prediction-market domain `agents/trading/prediction-market/` as empty folders only.

"The same" means: the acceptance checks at the end all pass.

You never:

- write a key value anywhere, open or read a `.env` file, or put a key in a doc, a setting or a log; key names only;
- create a trading account, a funded account or anything that can place a live order;
- write files inside `agents/trading/prediction-market/` other than `.gitkeep`, or give it agents, settings, scripts or docs: the domain is built in stage two from its own prompt;
- push, merge or publish without the owner's go.

Work in the build order below. Run each step's check before the next step. When this prompt says a point is open, leave what "Do not build" says in its place and ask the owner if you need it.

## Trading in brief

Trading is the first kind of work the Agent OS does, and everything about it lives below `agents/trading/`, so the system level stays general and knows nothing about money, accounts, markets or orders. `agents/trading/` is a folder of trading domains, not an agent: it has no AI instructions, settings, scripts or jobs of its own. It holds trading's own docs, the research studies the trading domains start from, and the trading domains.

A trading domain is one area of trading, such as prediction markets. It is a full domain of the Agent OS: a direct child of the system agent, reached through the system's `subagents.link/` folders. It arranges its agents in three levels, each with the standard agent folder: the domain agent; strategy agents, one per way to make money; and trading agents, also called variants, the versions of a strategy that trade, each with one set of changes, one AI model and one mode.

Every trading agent starts in test mode. Only the owner gives an agent an account with real money, and every new strategy configuration starts only after the owner reads a report on it and approves it. A change to a running agent makes a new test version with a new name. Orders are placed only on blockchains for now; centralised exchanges and other apps are sources of information only. Every order is logged.

The first trading domain is prediction markets on Polymarket, in `agents/trading/prediction-market/`. In stage one, the current stage, it is only its empty folders; its earlier files are kept in `vision/archive/2026-10-12/prediction-market/` and its trading notes in `vision/docs/prediction-market-agents/`. A later trading domain, such as copy trading, is a copy of it, made with `create-agent` when the owner asks.

## Ground rules

- **Safety.** No secret value anywhere. Keys are named in `.secrets/secrets.index.json` and their values live only in the git-ignored `.secrets/test/.env` and `.secrets/live/.env`, which you never open. Nothing you build can act outside the repository.
- **Formats.** Docs are Markdown. Settings and Details files are JSON, two-space indent, UTF-8, ending in a newline. No scripts are built at this level.
- **Names.** Folder and file names are lowercase with `-`, except the doc names `README.md`, `README.asd.md` and the research folders, which keep their names exactly as given, including `researches/` and `trding-agents-arhiteches/`.
- **Metadata next to every item.** Every file and folder you create has a How it works file (`[family].index.md`) and a Details file (`[family].meta.json`) next to it. The family is the file name without its last extension: `vision.md` gives `vision`, `README.asd.md` gives `README.asd`. A folder's metadata files sit inside it with the folder's name: `docs/docs.index.md`. Metadata files have no metadata of their own.
- **Example and Questions files.** Only the four docs in `agents/trading/docs/` also get `[family].example.md` (the doc's outline) and `[family].questions.md` (open questions for the owner about the doc).
- **Empty folders.** An empty folder holds one `.gitkeep`, so git keeps it. Remove the `.gitkeep` once the folder holds a real file.
- **Git.** Everything here is tracked. Nothing here is git-ignored.
- **Docs for people.** `vision.md`, `README.md` and `README.asd.md` contain no decision codes, input ids, `[n]` reference numbers or history. The owner is "the owner", and "they" as a pronoun.

## Conventions

- **Trading agent names** (decided rule, proposed format): `[strategy-id].[own-name]-v[N].[platform-model]-[test|live]`, lowercase `a-z`, `0-9`, `-` and `.`, at most 64 characters. `[strategy-id]` is the strategy agent's ID without `-agent` and its suffixes. Example: `pm-strategy-1.momentum-v1.opus55-test`. A trading agent's folder is named after it.
- **Strategy agent IDs** (default, the owner may change it): `[domain-code]-[strategy]-agent.[platform-model]-[test|live]`, for example `pm-strategy-1-agent.opus55-test`. The strategy folder keeps its plain name, `strategy-1-agent/`; the ID lives in the strategy's settings.
- **New versions.** A changed setting, instruction or script makes a new trading agent and raises `v[N]`; a different model changes `[platform-model]`. Names are never changed or reused.
- **Decision scripts** (default): a trading domain adds the script kind `decision` to the system's `worker` and `system`: `[name].decision.[ext]`, shared ones in the domain's `scripts/decisions/`.
- **Trading notes** (default): a trading domain's notes take a `trading-` prefix, so a trading agent's links to the system's notes and to its domain's never share a name.
- **Child links.** In every level with children, each content folder holds `subagents.link/[child-name]/`, a folder link to the child's folder of the same kind. The system's own `subagents.link/` folders point straight at `agents/trading/prediction-market/`; `agents/trading/` adds no level of agents. The `relink` script builds these links in stage two; in stage one the `[agent-name]/` placeholder folders stand in for them.

### How it works file

Front matter, then the six headings, in this order, each with one to four plain sentences or a short list, then up to four "Keep in mind" lines:

```markdown

node: n-56.1.2
written: 2026-10-12T00:00:00Z
by: knowledge-base-agent
---
# vision.md

## What it is
## Who looks after it
## When and how it changes
## Who uses it, and when
## Where it is mentioned
## Related knowledge

## Keep in mind

- When you ..., ...
```

The folder's own file may use one `## Summary` instead of the six headings.

### Details file

Every `.meta.json` has exactly these keys:

```json
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "about": "Trading's vision: why trading has its own place and what every trading domain shares.",
  "kind": "file",
  "state": "written",
  "status": "decided",
  "git": "tracked",
  "secret": false,
  "generated_by": null,
  "writers": ["knowledge-base-agent with the vision-doc skill", "the owner, on the File Tree page"],
  "readers": ["the owner", "every trading domain agent"],
  "changes_when": "an input changes what every trading domain shares",
  "related": [{"path": "agents/trading/docs/README.md", "how": "same words in In short"}],
  "sources": {"decisions": ["D-059"], "inputs": ["in-20261012-stage1"], "notes": []},
  "update_with": [{"path": "agents/trading/docs/README.md", "how": "bring In short in line"}],
  "inherits": [],
  "features": [],
  "views": [],
  "how_it_works": {"written": "2026-10-12T00:00:00Z", "by": "knowledge-base-agent"},
  "tree_number": "56.1.2"
```
